Apple has been historically late to the game in the smart-home world, if it bothers showing up at all. It’s had the most minimal smart speaker (and general smart home) offerings of any of the major brands, with just the HomePod and HomePod mini compared with the variety of speakers and smart home products Amazon and Google have launched in the past decade. A limited selection isn't necessarily a bad thing, but the Apple HomePods have also never excelled in our testing, either, and Apple's overall ecosystem has had the most limited compatibility compared with other devices (though Matter is helping expand that).
With the HomeView's arrival, Apple is making its first foray into the smart display category, nearly 10 years after Amazon’s first Echo Show model. While the HomeView manages to do some things well, it's once again a product made for only the biggest of Apple enthusiasts, and will shine best for users who have an iCloud subscription, love Apple Music, and will invest in Apple’s new, larger smart-home ecosystem , which has been designed in collaboration with LG and Schneider Electric. The HomeView does feel handy to use for making calls and sending texts—more so than any Amazon Echo Show ever was—and I love that I can use it to find my iPhone when I lose it around the house.
Still, I'd love to have been more impressed at this price point. After nearly two weeks of using the HomeView in my house, I find I use it most as a smart-home controller and to answer quick questions, and occasionally to FaceTime someone. Siri struggled to complete some of my music requests and took a long time to think about simple questions. Plus, some features on the device overall were roadblocked by my not having a full commitment to iCloud and Apple Photos. It's a device primarily for Apple devotees—especially the ones who will buy all of Apple's new smart-home products.
The most surprising thing to me is how small this device is. Maybe I've been overly influenced by the announcement of Amazon’s Echo Show 16 , which has a generous 16-inch display (hence the name), but the HomeView screen is just 7 inches and square, giving it a different look from most other smart displays, which go for a rectangular design. My colleague Julian Chokkattu described it as a “giant Apple Watch,” and I agree. The swiping side to side to switch between 10 different preloaded faces and the menu bar also feel incredibly similar to the Apple Watch.
Pressing and holding on the face of the HomeView allows you to customize your various “faces” (or remove them—it's a lot of options to have preloaded, in my opinion, and I found myself swiping through too frequently to find the smart home page). You can also click on the plus button to add other faces or informational pages like weather and views of your home cameras. But that's all you can add, at least for now. There's no app store, but the device can reflect certain apps from your phone, along with general apps you'd find on an Apple device like Safari, FaceTime, Messages, Find My, Alarms, and more. I was surprised to see Spotify, Libby, and Yoto specifically ported over from my phone, but no other non-Apple apps have made it over so far, at least from my own collection of downloaded apps.
There isn't a Siri AI app on the HomeView like on my iPhone, but the HomeView does use Siri AI to power its intelligence and answer your questions. You'll get a more conversational response than regular Siri, but I didn't find its answers to be that much more impressive. Siri ran into issues playing my music—it asks me whether the music should come from Books, TikTok, or Spotify if I don't specify, and then most of the time it still can't play the song on Spotify, even with my account set up. It also couldn't use Find My to find my iPhone when I asked. Both of these applications worked perfectly fine on the HomeView screen itself, but the on-device Siri isn't blowing me away thus far.
In fact, most things worked better by touch than voice. Spotify voice requests didn't seem to work, but the Spotify app on the device worked fine, as did using the handoff feature to send Spotify music from my phone to the HomeView. The Find My feature also didn't work over voice command—when I called my phone the same name I had seen it referred to on the HomeView while playing music, it claimed I had no device under that name. However, tapping the Find My app on the HomeView let me find my phone in a list of devices and tap it to make it start going off. While I'm bummed Siri won't let me just voice-request it, I am thrilled to have a faster way to find my iPhone lost in my house than pulling up iCloud.com.
I tested the HomeView with both an iPhone Air and an older iPhone 16 Pro , but you'll want a newer phone like the Air (or 17 Pro , 18 Pro , or iPhone Duo ) to get the most out of HomeView and Siri, since that's what gives you access to the expressive, customizable Siri voices. Switching to my original phone left me stuck with a boring Siri voice that I can't customize like I could when using the iPhone Air. No matter which phone you use, you'll also need to update your phone's operating system to OS 27.2.1 in order to set up and connect to the HomeView (which also brings Siri AI onto your phone, much to my husband's chagrin).
The main appeal of the HomeView, at least in my opinion, is the fact that it can control your smart-home devices with touch or voice. This is especially relevant since Apple is r olling out a larger smart-home ecosystem , with several devices coming later this year as part of its Apple Home Collection, including indoor and outdoor cameras, a smart thermostat, a video doorbell, a smart lock, and a couple of sensors. You can already control any Apple Home–compatible device on the HomeView, though, without needing Apple's lineup to release.
The HomeView provides a similar experience to other smart displays , with a page you can swipe to for accessing all of the devices set up through your Apple Home app. It's easy to see the devices and quickly control them. Apple Home's biggest issue, though, continues to be compatibility. Many smart devices are only Amazon- and Google-compatible, though Matter is fixing some of that issue; I was able to connect the Ikea Varmblixt ($100) smart lamp to my Apple Home app thanks to the Matter compatibility. It was fast and seamless to control once set up, both over voice and touch.
You can also touch to access your texts and FaceTime your contacts with the HomeView, which has been a pretty smooth experience for me. What's most interesting, though, is how the HomeView will verify that it's only you looking at your text messages. If it sees that someone else in your family is trying to look at or access your texts, it'll prompt that family member to switch over to their own account. It only works if they're alone in range of the device's camera, though; if they're peeking over your shoulder, access won't be denied.
Apple isn't using FaceID for this, surprisingly enough. It uses biometric data to figure out who's asking via a protected part of the processor Apple calls the Secure Exclave . It's a new technology that's also on the Apple Watch ; we'll have to see how it pans out in real time.
Of course, we can't talk about a smart display and speaker without talking about one of the key features: the speaker.
Sound is a big part of the enjoyment from this device, and while I enjoyed the audio quality, I found it frustrating to voice-request a song. When I asked for music without prompting which app it should come from, Siri asked me if I'd like it to come from Books, TikTok, or Spotify. And when I would request a song on Spotify, Siri would say I needed to “unlock my device,” but didn't specify if that needed to happen on my iPhone or my HomeView. Or it would simply tell me there was a problem and tell me to try again.

As businesses increasingly turn to AI agents to automate work, the vast amounts of information locked in complex documents remain a challenge. Unsiloed AI has raised $7.5 million in seed funding led by Felicis to tackle that problem, aiming to help enterprises make their documents more accessible to AI agents through specialized technology.
Silicon Valley venture capital firm Felicis led the round, with participation from Y Combinator, Orange Collective, and Uncorrelated Ventures. Angel investors Aarthi Ramamurthy and Beth Turner also participated.
Business documents often include tables, charts, and complicated layouts that AI systems can struggle to interpret accurately. But getting the information wrong can lead to costly mistakes for businesses, and the impact could be severe in the case of a bank, hospital, or a law firm, as they rely on these documents for their daily work.
Unsiloed aims to solve this problem with software that breaks down complex documents, extracts information from tables, charts and other elements, and turns it into structured data that AI agents can use. The technology also shows where the extracted information came from in the original document, so businesses can check the results rather than take the AI’s output at face value.
“The problem with LLMs is they’re inherently probabilistic,” said Unsiloed co-founder and CEO Aman Mishra (pictured above, right) in an interview. “There is going to be some deviation induced. There is going to be some hallucination involved, and that has a massive negative impact downstream.”
Mishra co-founded Unsiloed with Adnan Abbas (pictured above, left), his former classmate at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur. The two joined Y Combinator’s Fall 2025 batch after spending some time developing the technology.
Unsiloed is already working with customers in finance, legal services, and healthcare, Mishra told TechCrunch. One bank is using its technology to process documents, while a law firm has deployed it on its own servers to handle contracts and old case files, he said, without naming either customer. Mishra, however, named voice AI startup Bolna AI as a customer, saying it uses Unsiloed to ingest knowledge bases for building voice agents.
The San Francisco-headquartered startup has entered a market that is already crowded and includes specialized document-processing startups such as Reducto and Unstructured, as well as offerings from Microsoft and Amazon. Businesses also sometimes use general-purpose AI models to extract information from documents, giving Unsiloed another set of competitors.
Mishra told TechCrunch that Unsiloed’s advantage lies in how it processes complex documents. The startup uses what it calls “dual-stream” vision models, which handle text and image data separately, along with a technique called “heat map-based chunking” that helps identify the most important parts of a document.
“In one of the streams you have the text tokens, in the other stream you have the exact image tokens,” Mishra said. “This is something that we have spent a lot of time architecting.”
The technology then directs more computing power toward areas such as figures, numbers, and charts. Unsiloed also uses a specialized decoder that takes industry-specific terminology into account, helping it distinguish between terms that can mean different things in different business contexts.
Supporting those claims, Mishra pointed to a test involving 542 financial documents supplied by an enterprise customer. Unsiloed achieved 99.78% accuracy across roughly 84,000 extracted data points, per a technical brief shared by the startup. The test compared Unsiloed with major AI models, Microsoft’s Azure Document Intelligence, and the customer’s in-house extraction tool. The results have, however, not been independently verified.
Unsiloed also claims to have outperformed competing AI document-processing tools on olmOCR-Bench, a public benchmark developed by Allen AI. In tests conducted by the startup, Unsiloed scored 88.0, compared with 66.0 for Reducto’s agentic system and 39.9 for Unstructured. The benchmark covered 1,403 PDF pages and tested how well the systems handled tables, mathematical expressions, scanned documents, and complex layouts.
Unsiloed’s pricing, Mishra said, starts at one cent per page. He asserted that the startup’s approach also helps keep its costs down by directing computing power toward the parts of a document that need the most attention, instead of processing every section in the same way.
Currently, Unsiloed has a headcount of seven people. The startup, Mishra said, plans to use the fresh funding to hire more researchers and engineers, expand its sales efforts and develop proprietary datasets to improve its technology.

Jason and Lucia’s crime-heavy love story fuels a wonder of digital urban simulation.
Just a minute ago, I was shooting my way out of a cocaine deal gone wrong, darting behind furniture for cover. Now I’m sitting on the floor of my home, working through the instructions to construct an Ikea-style coffee table with my partner. A tiny heart with a plus sign pops up, showing that our relationship is stronger for this quotidian domestic effort.
This is the contrast at the heart of Grand Theft Auto VI , a game that seems to revel in both action movie bombast and the mundanities of everyday life for an up-and-coming young criminal couple.
The reimagined and expanded Vice City is still the grand, crude, satirical criminal playground you’d expect after 25 years of 3D Grand Theft Auto games. And that world is as full, detailed, technically impressive, and polished as you would expect after this latest installment received a reported billion-dollar budget and roughly a decade of development work involving thousands of Rockstar staffers.
But it’s the scenes between the over-the-top and somewhat repetitive action scenes that really make this Grand Theft Auto stand out. Almost every explosive gunfight or high-speed car chase is counterpointed by a sublimely dull, lightly interactive moment of mere routine existence: grilling burgers with pals by the water, playing fetch with a random dog, helping a neighbor tune up a car, or joking around over 18 holes of mini golf.
Taken together, the juxtaposition lends a sense of surreal hyperreality to the goings-on in Vice City and its environs. Each of the game’s two sides gives the other a chance to breathe, forming a series of emotional peaks and valleys that stretch across a truly gargantuan amount of detailed simulation and pure gaming content.
Grand Theft Auto VI never lets you get too settled with a budding life of crime or a budding family life. And it’s all the better for it.
A large part of why this works so well is Jason and Lucia, the dual protagonists whose relationship drives the story. While that relationship starts off a bit awkwardly—thanks chiefly to Lucia’s brief prison stint—it quickly develops into a true criminal and life partnership. Both sides of the relationship are driven by a mutual desire to move up in the criminal world and eventually settle down to a legit family life, if they can just earn enough from the next big score.
Of the two, Jason is definitely the duller partner. An ex-military meathead with a ripped body and a dull, affect-free vocal delivery, a decent chunk of Jason’s lines essentially boil down to “Yeah, sure, that’s fine.” While the game struggles to expose a bit of a tender and thoughtful side hiding underneath Jason’s cool demeanor, the writing can’t quite break through the emotionless masculine facade that Jason wears as a semi-permanent mask.
Lucia is much more interesting as a vivacious and amiable Latina eager to grab any opportunity presented to her. The game takes some time to dig into the difficulties of Lucia’s underprivileged youth and highlight her strained relationship with an unreliable mother, helping to add some important depth to her chip-on-her-shoulder journey of self-improvement. And even the boring Jason seems that much more appealing seen through the lens of Lucia’s good-natured teasing and genuine affection.
While Jason and Lucia can and do operate independently—and the game lets you change between them frequently—it’s their moments of togetherness that really stand out. There’s an easy, rom-com comfort to their time together, whether they’re discussing their future on the couch (“I feel like I haven’t done anything normal in a minute”), taking some time for quick romance (the game cuts away before things get too hot and heavy), or laying down covering fire for each other during a firefight (the lack of a co-op mode for these missions feels truly baffling).
There’s a minor relationship simulation component to the game, with a simple “heart level” that can rise or fall based on some basic decisions. Don’t expect a lot of dating-sim style drama, though; as long as you make the completely obvious choices when they’re presented, it’s hard to let the relationship fall apart. That’s a good thing, too, because this is a relationship that’s easy to root for, even when the participants are literally getting away with murder.
In true Grand Theft Auto fashion, Jason and Lucia’s particular way of chasing The American Dream is through a life of crime. Their travels through the criminal underworld start off kind of slow, as Lucia’s begging gradually compels Jason to reluctantly introduce her to the two-bit operators with which he’s found himself involved.
For the first half of the game, the pair are constantly interacting with a rogues’ gallery of new criminal acquaintances, each more over-the-top than the last, and all of them having specific needs that somehow only Jason and Lucia can fulfill. Many of the missions these small-time crooks have on offer end up feeling like the criminal equivalent of errands—drive here, take that, lose the cops, repeat.
And while a few standout characters develop complex interpersonal relationships with Jason and Lucia over multiple missions, most of these early side characters feel like one-note caricatures that can be distilled to a few tropey traits.
It isn’t until the back half of the game that the main storyline really starts to focus on what it does best: integrating Jason and Lucia into a persistent ring of professional criminals working toward bigger and bigger scores. Here, the missions build on each other, with characters going undercover, casing targets, and learning new skills that eventually come together in some truly tense and bombastic heists. These missions also do the best job of showing off the dual protagonist system, frequently shifting the perspective between Jason and Lucia to highlight their different skills and views on how things are going down.
Outside of this core plot, though, many of the missions and side stories in GTA VI make Jason and Lucia feel like side characters in their own story. I found myself beginning to tune out during some of the many missions in which one or both protagonists serve as glorified security props or overpaid getaway drivers amid other characters’ contrived turf wars. And even dozens of hours into the game, there were still missions that felt like tutorials, seemingly built around the opportunity to introduce some new simulation system or control scheme.
Through it all, the game can’t seem to totally shake the style of sophomoric humor that feels a lot less “edgy” today than it did when Grand Theft Auto III hit back in 2001 (for players who are old enough to remember that release , at least). There are countless extended bits where the entire joke seems to boil down to “Man, kinky sex is weird, isn’t it?” or “Hey look, it’s a male penis (or something that looks similar to one).” And the game seems to take particular pleasure in forcing Jason into uncomfortable situations with plenty of T&A, much to Lucia’s good-natured bemusement.
A word of warning for parents: This is a game that definitely earns a hard “M for Mature” rating and shows how standards for that rating have shifted since GTA: San Andreas earned an AO re-rating for hiding a single sex scene amid its legacy code.
There are moments where GTA VI ’s satire cuts a bit deeper. I especially liked a couple of side stories that skewered buzzword-spewing crypto bros and multi-level marketing schemes with some welcome over-the-top excess. Overall, though, the game’s warmed-over one-liner takes on “wokeness” felt about as fresh as jokes about mothers-in-law and TV dinners, without much in the way of thought-provoking statements on society as a whole in 2026.

Ankara'da uyuşturucu ticaretinden elde edilen suç gelirlerini çeşitli finansal işlemler, şirket faaliyetleriyle ve malvarlığı edinerek akladıkları tespit edilen ve "Çobanlar Grubu" olarak bilinen yapılanmanın firari lideri, 2 kişiyle birlikte yakalanarak gözaltına alındı.
İHA'nın haberine göre Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı koordinesinde Narkotik Suçlarla Mücadele Şube Müdürlüğünce uyuşturucu ticaretinden elde edilen suç gelirlerinin aklanmasına yönelik yürütülen soruşturma kapsamında 14 Kasım'da Ankara merkezli olarak geniş çaplı operasyon düzenlenmişti.
5237 sayılı Türk Ceza Kanunu’nun 282’nci maddesinde düzenlenen "suçtan kaynaklanan malvarlığı değerlerini aklama" suçu kapsamında yürütülen soruşturmada, MASAK raporu, saha araştırmaları ve finansal analizler sonucunda önemli bilgilere ulaşılmıştı.
Soruşturma kapsamında kamuoyunda "Çobanlar Grubu" olarak bilinen yapılanma içerisinde yer alan şüphelilerin uyuşturucu ticaretinden elde edilen suç gelirlerini çeşitli finansal işlemler, şirket faaliyetleri aracılığıyla ve malvarlığı edinerek akladıkları tespit edilmişti. Şüphelilere ait 18 araç, 12 gayrimenkul, 1 otel, 4 eğlence merkezi ve 1 ofis olmak üzere çok sayıda malvarlığına el konulmuştu. Şüphelilere ait şirketler ile bu şirketlere bağlı otel ve eğlence merkezlerinin toplam işlem hacminin 10 milyar 308 milyon 821 bin 634 lira olduğu belirlenmişti. Operasyon kapsamında 7 şüpheliye ait 6 ikamet ve 6 iş yerinde eş zamanlı arama ve el koyma işlemleri gerçekleştirilmiş, 4 şüpheli yakalanarak gözaltına alınmıştı. Operasyonda yakalanamayan yapılanmanın lideri B.Ç.’nin ise gece saatlerinde beraberindeki 2 kişiyle birlikte yakalanarak gözaltına alındığı öğrenildi.

Bursa ’da dini nikahla birlikte yaşadığı 2 çocuğunun annesi Arzu Khalılova’yı 146 makas darbesiyle öldürmekle suçlanan Salican Mehmet’in yargılandığı davada savcılık, sanığın ağırlaştırılmış müebbet hapisle cezalandırılmasını talep etti. Sanık ise pişman olduğunu belirterek tahliyesini istedi.
DHA'daki habere göre olay; 3 Kasım 2025’te saat 15.00 sıralarında Bursa’nın Yıldırım ilçesindeki evde meydana geldi. Arzu Khalılova ile dini nikahla birlikte yaşadığı Salican Mehmet arasında çıkan tartışma, kavgaya dönüştü. Mehmet, 4 ve 1 yaşlarındaki 2 kızının annesi Khalılova’ya makasla saldırdı.
Alt katta oturan ve sesleri duyup üst kata çıkan Salican Mehmet’in annesi F.M., Arzu Khalılova’nın yerde yattığını görünce durumu eşi İ.M.’ye bildirdi. İ.M.’nin ihbarı üzerine adrese polis ve sağlık ekipleri sevk edildi.
Mehmet elinde makasla yakalanırken, yaralı olarak ambulansla Bursa Yüksek İhtisas Eğitim ve Araştırma Hastanesi’ne kaldırılan Khalılova hayatını kaybetti.
Otopside Khalılova'nın vücudunun değişik yerlerinde toplam 146 makas girişi olduğu, bunların 72'sinin tek başına ölümcül nitelikte olduğu belirlendi. Cenaze, işlemlerinin ardından toprağa verildi.
Emniyetteki ifadesinde; Arzu Khalılova ile 4 yıldan beri dini nikahla birlikte yaşadıklarını söyleyen Salican Mehmet, psikolojik problemleri olduğunu ve tedavi gördüğünü iddia ederek, "Son birkaç aydır bende ruhsal açıdan sıkıntılar olmaya başladı.
Bundan dolayı yaklaşık 2 ay önce Bursa'da Ruh ve Sinir Hastalıkları Hastanesine yatarak tedavi görmeye başladım. Burada yaklaşık 21 gün tedavi gördüm ve taburcu edildim. Taburcu edildiğimde bana günde 3 defa kullanılmak üzere ilaç verildi.
Ben bu ilaçları bir süre kullandım. Bu süre zarfında eşimle kavgalarımız oldu, birbirimizi darp ettik ancak birbirimizden şikayetçi olmamıştık. Eşimle tartıştığımız zaman bazen benim gözüm döner ve ne yaptığımı bilemem, birden parlardım. Ancak eşimle ciddi bir sorunumuz yoktu" dedi.
İfadesinde; olaydan 1 gün önce eşiyle küçük kızlarının ağlaması nedeniyle tartıştıklarını ve birbirlerini darp ettiklerini söyleyen Mehmet, "Olay günü büyük kızım babaannesine gitti. Bebeğimiz evdeydi. Eşim çamaşırları topluyordu.
Bana ‘Çocuğa bak’ dedi. Ben de ‘Bakıyorum’ dedim. Bana hala ‘Çocuğa bak’ deyince, dünden de kavgalı olduğumuz için sinirlendim. O sırada benim yine gözüm karardı. Daha sonra çocuk odasına gittim. Çocuğa baktım ve orada bulunan makası aldım. Ondan sonra salona geldim.
Direkt eşime makasla saldırmaya başladım. Makasla birçok kez saldırdım ama ne kadar olduğunu bilmiyorum. Bunun üzerine eşim yere yığıldı" ifadelerini kullandı.
Emniyetteki işlemlerinin ardından sevk edildiği adliyede çıkarıldığı mahkemede tutuklanan Salican Mehmet’in 'Kasten yaralama’, ‘Kullanmak için uyuşturucu bulundurma’, ‘Ateşli silahlar kanununa muhalefet’ suçlarından 8 kaydı olduğu, yine öldürdüğü Arzu Khalılova’ya yönelik eylemi nedeniyle hakkında 'Reşit olmayanla cinsel ilişki' suçundan işlem yapıldığı ortaya çıktı.
Hakkında 'Kadına karşı kasten öldürme’ suçundan ağırlaştırılmış müebbet hapis istemiyle dava açılan Mehmet’in, yargılanmasına Bursa 19’uncu Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi’nde devam edildi. Duruşmaya tutuklu sanık ile Arzu Khalılova’nın annesi Zülfiye Halil, sanığın babası İ.M. ve taraf avukatları katıldı.
Önceki duruşmada istenen İstanbul Adli Tıp Kurumu Gözlem İhtisas Dairesi’nden gelen sanığın akli melekelerinin yerinde olduğuna dair rapor için söz verilen sanık, pişman olduğunu ve olay anında kendinde olmadığını dile getirerek tahliyesini talep etti.
Salican Mehmet’in savunmasının ardından Cumhuriyet savcısı mütalaasını verdi. Savcı, 72’si iç organlara gelecek ve tek başına ölümcül olmak üzere toplamda 146 makas darbesiyle ölümün gerçekleştirilmesi nedeniyle sanığını ‘Canavarca hisle kadına karşı kasten öldürme suçu’ndan ağırlaştırmış müebbet hapse çarptırılmasını talep etti.
Mütalaayı kabul etmediklerini dile getiren sanık Salican Mehmet’in avukatı, İstanbul Adli Tıp Kurumu Raporu’na itiraz ederek yeniden rapor düzenlenmesini talep ederek, mütalaaya karşı ek süre talep etti. Mahkeme heyeti, sanık avukatının ek süre talebini kabul ederek duruşmayı erteledi.

$25 doesn’t go as far as it used to. As recently as a decade ago, $25 could fill up your gas tank and buy a pretty good gift, with plenty of options for just about every interest and occasion. Nowadays, it’s a struggle to even find a $25 takeout meal for one person and average national gas prices are inching toward $5 a gallon . And we all know wages have not kept up.
Good news: There are still plenty of thoughtful, interesting items out there to be had for $25, which are sure to appeal to everyone from coworkers to neighbors, relatives you don’t know well, and the friend who seems to have everything. All things on this list have been tested and vetted by at least one person on the WIRED Reviews team—often more than one—to ensure it is indeed a good gift you’d be proud to give. Check out more of our gift guides to find something for everyone on your list this year.
Love WIRED ? Add us as a preferred source on Google to see more of us.
WIRED senior Gear editor Julian Chokkattu recommends this colorful acrylic desk accessory that keeps pencils, scissors, and other large items on top and smaller items like paper clips (or, in Julian’s case as a phone reviewer , SIM ejection pins) on the bottom. Shown is the pink-and-amber color combination, but there’s also a blue-and-green option.
I’ve used Field Notes for years—they’re lightweight, sturdy, and a perfectly pocketable. The National Parks Series elevates what would otherwise be a utilitarian notebook to its giftable status, with artist-created covers inspired by our nation’s natural wonders—from Acadia to the Hawaii Volcanoes.
My city recently got its own brick-and-mortar Muji store, and if you’ve never visited the famed Japanese retailer in person, it’s basically a mecca for stationery and desk accessories. These pens in particular are famous for their smooth ink and precision tips, and make a perfect companion for the Field Notes notebooks at left.
These drink cozies are a favored white elephant gift from WIRED reviewer Nena Farrell (“It’s like playing Barbie with your drinks,” she says), but I like them because they remind me of Will Ferrell and his friend Harper Steele in the movie Will & Harper, where they go on a road trip, dress up their drinks in these exact cozies, and come up with ridiculous names for them like Cornelius Danderhoff. It reminds me of road trips I took with friends in college, which reminds me that I’m old, which … makes me want a drink.
Set the right vibe in any room with this WIRED-recommended , Matter-compatible smart light bulb that features millions of colors, scenes, and effects you can control with Alexa, Google Assistant, or the Govee app. You can also sync it to music with the latter, using the microphone on your phone.
Let your giftee be heard wherever they go with their very own Bluetooth microphone. Former WIRED A/V editor Parker Hall especially liked this one for its series of playback and mixing controls, in addition to adjustable volume, echo effects, and the ability to play, skip, or pause your backing track.
A sleep mask is a must for proper sleep hygiene, and WIRED reviewer and sleep mask aficionado Louryn Strampe loves the roomy fit of this 22-momme silk model from Quince. It’s half the price of similar 100-percent silk sleep masks, and there’s free shipping to keep things affordable. Choose from among 12 color options, including Eucalyptus, Espresso, Pink, Terra Cotta, and Light Blue.
Crowned our best earplugs for sleep , the silicone Loop Quiet 2 are capable of blocking out 24 dB and fit entirely flush with your head, ensuring that they’re perfectly comfortable when you lie on your side. The little handle makes them easy to pull out, and they come in four fun colors with a variety of ear tips to ensure your giftee can get the perfect fit.
Help your giftee’s personal space stay cool and fresh with this 4-in-1 fan, the best handheld fan I’ve personally tried . You can set it on a table or desk, hold it in your hand, clip it onto something with the bottom carabiner, or wear it around your neck. It’s plenty quiet enough to hold a conversation over, and it comes in four fun colors.
My entire family is obsessed with this finishing salt, which is harvested in Netarts Bay, Oregon, just a couple of hours from our house. The large, irregular crystals look (and taste) fantastic on meat, roast vegetables, and desserts, and offer the perfect amount of crunch. Either the salt itself or the stylish arched salt cellar—handmade by Pigeon Toe Ceramics in Portland, Oregon—would make a terrific gift on its own.
A sharp, trusty chef’s knife is a staple in any kitchen, and Kiwi knives are beloved by multiple members of the WIRED Reviews team for their ability to hold an edge just as well as knives that cost 10 times as much. I’ve had a Kiwi knife in my own knife drawer for more than 20 years, and it’s still going strong.
Who doesn’t love a colorful Le Creuset Dutch oven? The real-deal, enameled cast iron version may not be in your gifting budget, but the 8-ounce stoneware cocotte is perfect as a salt cellar, garlic roaster, or even a bowl to eat out of. Most of the classic colors are available, so you can match your giftee’s kitchen or other Le Creuset pots if they have them.
I have a separate gift guide for plant lovers , where I talk about how much I like the usability of this book. Put together by Vanessa Minton of From the Garden , “How to Grow Medicinal Herbs” features clear and complete directions that are perfect for beginners, from growing the plants to how to incorporate them into infused oils, tinctures, teas, and syrups. I actually did give a copy to a friend as a gift, and she liked it so much she took it on a trip and read it cover to cover on the plane.
I received this dehydrated fruiting block in a box for my birthday a couple of years ago, and I was super impressed with how quickly and abundantly the oyster mushrooms grew—right on my windowsill. Growing mushrooms isn’t always easy , but this is a fun and educational method for kids and adults alike.
Tropical Monstera deliciosa houseplants are all the rage right now, but many people may not know that they actually bear a fruit. It’s rarely produced outside the monstera’s native climate, so you may not have the opportunity to taste it, but you can get the gist with this one-of-a-kind monstera fruit taffy. (It’s tart!)
Being able to keep track of keys, luggage, and other gear is critical, and these Bluetooth trackers work just as well as AirTags for a quarter of the price. A pack of four with little lanyards and fun stickers retails for $24 but often on sale for even less. They work with Apple’s Find My and take just seconds to sync to your phone. I have four of these in use in my household, and they are truly indistinguishable from AirTags in both tracking and quality. There’s also a rechargeable set that works with both iOS and Android, but we haven’t tried that one.
WIRED contributing reviewer Alexis Berger organized multiple zones of her house with these QR Code stickers. They come with a free app that will scan and catalog all of a drawer or box’s contents using AI—that way you can just look on your phone for the location of an item instead of spending all day tearing your home and garage apart.
I cannot even begin to list all the times I’ve been glad to be carrying a reusable bag, but the ones I usually have in my purse are small and flimsy. Former WIRED reviewer Medea Giordano loved this 25-inch-tall ripstop model that carries up to 50 pounds yet folds into a flat 5-by-5-inch pouch. It’s also machine washable and comes in 35 colors and prints.
WIRED contributing reviewer and former barista Pete Cottell loves this espresso accessory for its durability and design—and can be found in seemingly every coffee shop where I live in the Pacific Northwest. However, even if you don’t have an espresso machine, the uses for a little spouted measuring cup are endless. I have a plastic one and use it for everything from mea…

Apple ’ın iCloud, App Store ve Apple Music başta olmak üzere çeşitli servisleri, 17 Kasım’da yaşanan teknik kesinti nedeniyle bir süre kullanılamadı. Şirketin Sistem Durumu sayfasında iCloud Hesap ve Giriş hizmetlerinde tüm kullanıcıları etkileyen sorunlar listelenirken App Store, AppleCare on Device ve Apple Music’te de kesintiler görüldü.
iCloud tarafındaki sorunlar, kullanıcıların Apple hesaplarına giriş yapmasını zorlaştırdı. Bazı kullanıcılar iPhone’larında yeniden Apple Kimliği parolası istenmesiyle karşılaşırken Apple hesabıyla diğer servislere giriş yapamadı. Sosyal medyada paylaşılan bildirimlere göre yeni iPhone’ların etkinleştirilmesinde de sorun yaşandı.
Kesinti Apple’ın perakende operasyonlarını da etkiledi. NBC News’e konuşan New York ve Chicago’daki Apple Store çalışanları, mağazaların dahili yazılımlarının çalışmadığını, bu nedenle satın alma işlemlerinin tamamlanamadığını ve randevu oluşturulamadığını aktardı. Gün içinde Apple’ın sistem durumu sayfasına Apple Business, Apple School Manager, AppleCare, iCloud Mail, iCloud Web Apps ve Schoolwork hizmetlerindeki sorunlar da eklendi.
Apple, kesintinin bir iç güncellemeden kaynaklandığını ve siber saldırı olmadığını açıkladı. Şirket, sabah saatlerinde yaşanan sorunun ardından sistemlerinin büyük bölümünün yeniden çalışır hale geldiğini, kalan servisleri de mümkün olan en kısa sürede devreye almak için çalıştığını belirtti . Apple’ın durum sayfasına göre kesintiler 17 Kasım’da ABD saatiyle 18.00 itibarıyla giderildi. Kesinti, son günlerde ABD’de e-posta, hava ulaşımı ve çevrim içi bankacılık gibi alanlarda yaşanan teknik aksaklıkların ardından geldi. Söz konusu olayların birbiriyle bağlantılı olduğuna dair bir bulgu paylaşılmadı.

As demand grows for real-world data to train robots, India’s Humyn Labs has raised $47 million in Series A financing to help U.S. AI and robotics companies build models that can operate in physical environments.
The funding comprises $26 million in equity led by Accel, with participation from Prosus Ventures, BeeGlobal, Bajaj Finance’s Finserv Intelligence and Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, Dallas Venture Capital, Lighthouse Canton, and Jump Trading. It also includes $21 million in venture debt led by Lighthouse Canton Growth Debt Fund II, with participation from Trifecta Capital.
Companies around the world are trying to build robots capable of performing everyday human tasks , but getting enough quality data to train them remains difficult. Startups including Mecka AI , XDOF , and MicroAGI are already tackling the problem by collecting real-world data for robotics training. Bengaluru-based Humyn Labs aims to compete with them.
Humyn Labs has developed its own two-camera hardware to record people performing everyday tasks. It then uses its software to process and label the footage, which means tagging what happens in each clip so AI can learn from it. The startup collects data across over 20 countries in Latin America and Asia, with Brazil, India, and South Korea serving as its main hubs, co-founder Manish Agarwal (pictured above, right) said in an interview.
Agarwal, the former CEO of Indian gaming company Nazara Technologies, founded Humyn Labs in February with Ishank Gupta (pictured above, left), a former executive at the brewing giant AB InBev. The duo previously founded Kratos Studios, now known as KGeN . KGeN has a network of contributors across emerging markets, and that network helps Humyn Labs collect data in people’s homes, the founders told TechCrunch.
Collecting footage of human activity is only part of the challenge, Agarwal said. He added that Humyn Labs also uses software to track hand movements, interactions with objects, and other details, turning raw recordings into data that AI models can learn from.
“Scale, diversity, and quality are important aspects, and they need to work in tandem,” Agarwal said.
Humyn Labs says it has 12 paying customers, including frontier AI labs, robotics companies, and developers of world models. About 90% of its revenue comes from the U.S., Gupta said, though he declined to name specific customers.
The startup generated $10 million in revenue between April and October and has another $20 million in signed contracts, Agarwal told TechCrunch, adding that a further $20 million in deals has yet to be finalized.
That growth has also increased Humyn Labs’ need for working capital, Agarwal said, explaining the $21 million venture debt component. The startup pays workers and data collection partners daily or weekly but typically waits 30 to 60 days to receive payments from its AI lab customers. Borrowing helps bridge that gap and is less dilutive than selling more equity, he said.
Over the last few months, India has emerged as a hub for collecting training data for so-called physical AI, with startups including Human Archive and BuildAI tapping into the country’s large workforce to record people performing everyday tasks. However, the practice has also raised questions about privacy and consent, particularly when people are recorded inside their homes.
Agarwal said Humyn Labs collects data from people doing their usual work or household chores instead of asking them to perform staged activities. The startup works with local partners to identify collection sites and oversee the process. “The worker is a worker who is incentivized, but he needs to be monitored and supervised for the right input,” he stated.
Humyn Labs currently has 51 full-time employees, most based in Bengaluru, plus a network of local partners across the countries where it collects data, Agarwal said.

Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are holding talks in Shenzhen, a day before a one-of-its-kind trilateral summit with US President Donald Trump in the southern Chinese city.
Chinese and Russian news agencies reported that the two leaders began talks around midday on Wednesday.
It was their fifth meeting this year, one of which took place by video link.
Thursday’s meeting has raised concern in Kyiv and European capitals that the three leaders could settle Ukraine’s future without them and divide the world into modern spheres of influence.
Washington initially said Ukraine was not expected to be on the agenda, but Trump later said it would be. Xi regards the war as not China’s concern.
Beijing has said only that the leaders will hold “in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations” on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting.
According to Washington, the Iran war and nuclear disarmament are also on the table after the US-Russia bilateral nuclear weapons treaty expired in February. China has long argued that the US and Russia should cut their much larger arsenals before it will discuss limits on its own.
Opening the event, Xi called for stronger international cooperation on artificial intelligence and free trade. China would pursue “deep-seated reform”, he said, starting with lower tariffs, wider market access and work on regulation and management standards.
Putin, who has been shunned by the West since he invaded Ukraine in 2022, told the APEC gathering he expected the trilateral to be “highly useful”.
With military and political risks rising, he said, “what is desperately needed is unity rather than division... and dialogue rather than ultimatums.”
He also argued that Western sanctions had failed, saying they could not fully halt growth or wreck the economies of rival states.
Trump was still in the Philippines on Wednesday, where he attended a summit of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). A day earlier he met fellow Quad leaders from Australia, Japan and India for the first time in his second term. The group is broadly seen as a counterweight to Chinese influence in the region.
He said he hoped to hold one-on-one talks with both Putin and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in Shenzhen, adding that Kim “would like” to meet in China.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking in Manila, stopped short of confirming a Kim meeting but said engagement was the only way to resolve problems with North Korea.
Around 2,000 people protested during Trump’s visit, carrying banners reading “Trump out now” and “Reject Pax Silica”, a reference to a US supply chain initiative.

Democrat Mary Peltola flipped the US Senate seat in Alaska on Tuesday after a tight race that unseated Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan, according to the official ballot count.
With 50.12% of the vote, Peltola's win means the US Senate will have a 56-44 Democratic majority, clinching the chamber's last open race in a midterm election that crushed Republicans across the country and handed US President Donald Trump a firm rebuke of his second term.
"As our next United States Senator, I will stand up to anyone to take on the rigged system in DC and deliver results for Alaska's working families," Peltola said in a statement late on Tuesday.
"As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my life to serving our state, there is no greater honour than having Alaskans' support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs and put Alaska first."
With far-flung rural voters in remote villages, the vote count in Alaska took two weeks to complete, but offered Peltola a strong mandate.
With 144,302 votes, Peltola beat Sullivan's 131,844 votes, even when combined with a second candidate named Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. who earned 4,760 votes.
Trump had called for another Republican candidate in the race, Gerald Heikes, to have his votes "immediately given" to Dan S. Sullivan, calling it the "fair solution."
Heikes won 6,105 votes in the race, but merging all the votes that Trump wanted to combine would still not have been enough to beat Peltola.
The Alaska Senate race had attracted national attention following a New York Times investigation revealing that aides to Peltola had recruited another man named Dan Sullivan to run for office with the goal of siphoning votes from the Republican incumbent.
"My opponent's campaign is literally focused on misleading Alaskans, lying and cheating," Senator Sullivan told reporters in Anchorage on election day.
The fact that there were two candidates named Dan Sullivan had repeatedly drawn the ire of Trump, who said Democrats had used a "decoy" to siphon votes from the Republican candidate.
The Trump administration had gone so far as to ask the courts to block certification of the results if the incumbent Sullivan lost because of the potential mix-up.
The legal bid, which Trump has said he ordered personally, sparked alarm in political circles, but was dismissed by a federal judge ahead of the election.
However, US Attorney Michael Heyman claimed federal investigators were conducting both criminal and civil probes involving the Alaska Senate race.
Peltola's historic victory makes her one of the first two Native American women ever to be elected to the US Senate, where she will join Minnesota Senator-elect Peggy Flanagan.
Democrats will control 56 seats in the 100-seat Senate which will give them the power to block legislation, launch broad investigations into Trump's administration and thwart his judicial and senior government appointments.

Democrat Mary Peltola defeated Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska on Tuesday, completing a political comeback in a state that US President Donald Trump has repeatedly won by wide margins. Her victory gives Democrats a 56-44 Senate majority, marking their biggest net gain in Senate seats since 1958.
Democrat Mary Peltola defeated two-term Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska, overcoming allegations that members of her campaign helped recruit a candidate who shares the incumbent’s name and completing a political comeback in a state President Donald Trump repeatedly won by wide margins.
The Alaska race is the last US Senate contest to be resolved in this year's midterm elections , and Peltola’s victory expands the Democrats’ majority after they retook control of the chamber. The party already won campaigns in conservative states including South Carolina, Texas, Kansas and, most recently, Mississippi.
With Peltola’s victory, Democrats flipped nine Senate seats, the most since 1958. Republicans entered the midterms with a 53-47 majority, while Democrats now emerge with a 56-44 margin.
Messages seeking comment were left with both campaigns Tuesday night.
Read more 'Climate action is alive': Triumphant Democrats attend COP31 summit shunned by Trump
Peltola, in a statement on social media, said there “is no greater honour than having Alaskans’ support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs and put Alaska first. Thank you, Alaska. Let’s get to work.”
Alaska also elected a Democrat as governor for the first time since 1998, after former state lawmaker Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins defeated three Republicans , including one endorsed by Trump. The Associated Press has not yet called the US House race, where independent candidate Bill Hill is challenging Republican Rep. Nick Begich.
Peltola previously held the state's lone House seat, making her the first Alaska Native to serve in Congress . She lost her bid for a second full term to Begich in 2024, but she became central to Democrats’ plans to retake the Senate in 2026.
In the campaign’s final stretch, however, she faced allegations that her team helped recruit a retired teacher named Dan J. Sullivan to run in order to siphon votes from the incumbent.
Read more Democrat Scott Colom wins historic Senate race in Mississippi
Trump called for Peltola’s prosecution after The New York Times first reported the allegation less than a week before the November 3 election. Peltola denied any involvement.
“I knew nothing about any other candidates on the ballot except for me and the incumbent,” Peltola told supporters in Juneau days before the election.
Dan J. Sullivan has denied any contact with Peltola’s campaign or running at the Democrats' behest. He has not responded to messages from The Associated Press since The Times’ article was published.
The Times report was based partly on text messages and other documents and interviews with Peltola’s former campaign manager, who was fired shortly before this year’s open primary and later sought to recant her statements. But the second Sullivan had already been on Trump’s mind. He referred to him multiple times during a rally in support of the senator in mid-October.
Later, the Department of Justice filed a lawsuit that Trump said he ordered. It sought to block certification of the race if the incumbent were to lose, pending an investigation into possible voter confusion. Peltola called the lawsuit “flagrant corruption ”.

The case was dismissed by a federal judge, but the Justice Department appealed. Attorneys for the state sought dismissal, saying officials should be able to conduct the election “without unwarranted interference by the United States ". They also argued the ballot was designed to distinguish the two Sullivans as much as possible and that Alaska’s ranked choice voting process would allow any voters who might be confused to rank them.
The Justice Department also confirmed the existence of a criminal investigation, but Alaska’s US attorney would not say what potential crimes authorities were looking into.
Peltola finished first in the primary with 49.5% of the vote, followed by the incumbent with 41.4%.
Dan J. Sullivan finished a distant third with about 2.5%, but he advanced to the general election as one of the top four finishers. He was listed on both ballots as Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., with no party affiliation, while the senator was listed as Dan S. Sullivan, Republican and incumbent.
During the campaign, Peltola tapped into Alaskans’ frustrations with high fuel prices and other costs. Those concerns hit especially hard in remote communities that rely on diesel for electricity and heat and are often only accessible by air or water.
Her campaign peppered social media with photos of her travels around the state as she sought to separate herself from national Democrats and build a coalition of support around a platform of “Alaska first”.
“Alaskans who know me know that I’m not liberal or radical,” Peltola said. “I am only interested in working for Alaska and working for the best interest of Alaskans, in as nonpartisan of a way as I possibly can.”
The race attracted a flood of spending by outside groups and at times turned negative, with the campaigns accusing each other of spreading lies. Trump and Vice President JD Vance made separate trips to the state in the month before the election in support of the incumbent.
“Lower 48” became something of an insult bandied by both sides. Sullivan and his supporters tried to align Peltola with “Lower 48 liberals” who want to restrict oil and gas drilling, mining and other resource development in the state. Peltola said that while she would work with Trump to get things done for Alaska, “I will never put any Lower 48 politician before Alaskans. That’s the difference between Dan and me.”
When Sullivan took issue with Peltola reading off note cards during a debate – “You can’t cue-card your way to the Senate,” he told reporters – Peltola said she simply was prepared. She also pushed back against Sullivan’s assertion that she was ineffective during her time in the House, saying she worked well with him as part of the state’s three-person delegation in Washington .
Peltola postponed two days of campaign events in late October after her campaign said she suffered minor injuries in a car accident in Anchorage.
Peltola, who is Yup’ik, emphasised her Alaska roots and resurrected the “fish, family and freedom” tagline from her prior campaigns. She spoke about growing up in western Alaska and fishing for salmon on the Kuskokwim River with her father and spending parts of the summer at fish camp with her children and late husband, who died in September 2023.
She said the fish and wildlife that Alaskans long relied on to fill their freezers for the winter were becoming harder to find. The changes were forcing people to buy more food and other staples at the store – supplies that must be barged or flown in – and deal with “crushing prices", she said.
Peltola also said she saw members of Congress who were “more focused on their stock portfolios” than helping ease those costs and vowed to push back against the billionaire class.
Peltola will be just the fifth Democrat since statehood to represent Alaska in the Senate. The most recent was Mark Begich, whom Sullivan defeated in 2014.

Mobile gamers don’t have many dedicated gaming smartphones to choose from, so Nubia’s Redmagic series stands out. This big, boxy phone offers cutting-edge performance, long battery life, and a large display. You also get touch-sensitive shoulder buttons, RGB lighting, and gaming-focused software features.
Sadly, Nubia has followed every other phone manufacturer this year, offering minimal iterative improvements while jacking up the price significantly. While this series has always been a clear bargain for gamers seeking the best chipset, it’s harder to swallow the compromises lurking here (camera, software, update commitment) when the price starts at $949.
The Nubia Redmagic 12 Pro sports the same boxy design as its predecessors, just a teeny bit slimmer and lighter. I’m a fan of the translucent industrial aesthetic and RGB lighting, but it’s not something I really want in my everyday phone. I had exactly the same issues with the 12 Pro as I had with the 10 Pro I reviewed two years ago. It’s very big, so you really feel it in your pocket, and it can be awkward to handle, especially when you’re trying to scroll one-handed. It’s also the most slippery phone ever. Every time I put it down, the 12 Pro slowly starts to slide away.
The big positive of this design is that it feels great in landscape orientation for gaming. The thick frame is easy to hold. There are touch-sensitive shoulder buttons on the top edge, and Nubia has a dedicated Magic Key for gaming mode, though you can customize it to launch the camera. This used to be a switch, but is now a red button. It’s still flanked by the round power button. Sadly, there’s no headphone port.
It’s refreshing not to have a camera bump on the back, though this inevitably adds to the slipperiness, and this glass sandwich quickly gets covered in finger smudges. Nubia has toned down the lighting a little, but you can still customize it for all sorts of activities. There’s a powerful cooling fan inside, with two vents to expel hot air, but the 12 Pro still somehow scores an IP68/69 rating for dust and water resistance.
The 6.85-inch OLED display is completely uninterrupted, with no notch or cutout camera to break it up. There’s an effective fingerprint sensor at the bottom and a less effective selfie camera under the top of the screen. The screen can hit a 185-Hz refresh rate , but only a handful of games actually support it. Most of the time you’ll be capped at 120 Hz. It supports HDR with 5,000-nit local peak brightness for highlights, but overall brightness is capped at 1,900 nits. Overall, it’s a lovely display, and a pleasure to play games or watch movies on. The Dolby Atmos–certified stereo speakers are decent for a phone.
Perhaps the biggest enticement is Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset, paired with Redmagic’s RedCore R5 chipset and 12 or 16 GB of RAM. You won’t find a faster Android phone right now, and the Redmagic 12 Pro can even give the iPhone 18 Pro a run for its money. Benchmark scores topped the Android charts, above phones like Samsung’s Galaxy S26 Ultra .
I had no issues playing Asphalt Legends and Wuthering Waves with settings cranked to the max. I also tried PUBG Mobile , one of the titles that can support that 185-Hz refresh rate, and it was smooth sailing. The 12 Pro keeps its cool, even after an hour or so of challenging gaming. Aside from the fan and vapor chamber for cooling, Nubia added dual-loop liquid cooling. You do get some fan noise and thermal throttling, but the 12 Pro has enough grunt to satisfy even the most hardcore of gamers.
Nubia includes a dedicated game space called Gravity X, triggered by that red button, where you can map those pressure-sensitive shoulder buttons and optimize the settings for your favorite games. It’s packed with options and even includes an anime companion and AI assistant called Mora. Even more exciting, it has an embedded Steam emulator, so you can log into your account and potentially play Steam games on the 12 Pro, though not everything works. It’s also easy to connect a gamepad, mouse, and keyboard, or a second screen.
To keep you gaming for longer, the 12 Pro boasts an enormous 8,400-mAh battery. Even with hours of gaming, I made it to the end of every day with something left in the tank. With careful use, you could easily push this phone to two days. There’s no charger in the box, but it supports up to 80-watt wired or wireless charging if you spring for a Redmagic charger. It took me an hour and 17 minutes to charge it from dead, but you can hit around 50 percent in half an hour. Sadly, it doesn’t support Qi2 magnets , so you’ll need a flat wireless charging pad.
To get top-notch performance at this price, you’ll have to accept several compromises. Let’s start with the camera. While the main 50-megapixel camera is quite good, and there’s a 50-megapixel ultrawide, the flat design doesn’t leave room for a telephoto lens, so you can only get 2X zoom by cropping. The main camera will satisfy folks who only snap the odd photo, and it does well in most conditions. The ultrawide is fine for group shots, but its smaller sensor means performance suffers in low light. The 16-megapixel front-facing camera is hidden under the screen, and it’s fine for video calls or well-lit selfies, though shots often look a bit muddy.
The real problem with the 12 Pro’s camera is the processing. Use the terrible portrait mode or zoom in too far and you’ll see how badly it handles image processing. Nubia lacks Google’s expertise in this space, so a camera system that sounds similar on paper produces far worse photos in reality. Nubia’s colors often look a bit off, it really struggles with mixed lighting, and shots tend to be noisy or oversharpened. Video recording is quite good with the main camera, but stabilization was a little poor in some of the videos I shot.
Another big turnoff with the 12 Pro is the software. Redmagic OS 12 sits atop Android 17, and it’s mostly OK, though I wish Chinese manufacturers didn’t feel the need to imitate things like Apple’s Liquid Glass. The interface also has some bad translations. What’s worse is the prevalence of absolute junk bloatware and the subpar update commitment. Nubia is only promising two years of platform updates and three years of security software updates in the US (five years in the UK).
Our best Android phones guide includes many more well-rounded options than the 12 Pro. You can even buy a Pixel 11 Pro XL on sale for the same price right now. But the 12 Pro is all about gaming, and to that end, it offers the best performance-and-screen combo you can get today. Whether the gaming features, cooling tech, and overall style add enough value depends on you. That same chipset will roll into more phones soon, and most of them will have a better camera and longer software support, but they’re likely to be more expensive, like the forthcoming Motorola Signature 27 at $1,600 .
For buyers in the US, check your carrier bands. The 12 Pro should be fine with T-Mobile and its associated MVNOs, but it may not work well, or at all, with some other carriers. It also doesn’t support eSIM, so you need a physical SIM card. The 12-GB RAM and 256-GB storage model is $949; upgrading to 16 GB and 512 GB costs $1,049, and the 1-TB model is $1,199.
texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmy4:
Gas and electricity bills are forecast to jump by £443 a year from January as energy costs continue to push up the UK's inflation rate.
The annual price cap on gas and elecrtricity is predicted to rise by 26% in the new year, according to researchers at consultancy Cornwall Insight. Energy regulator Ofgem will announce the new cap next Wednesday, 25 November.
A sharp jump means inflation is at risk of continuing to rise - official data revealed prices rose 3.6% in the year to October, up from 3.5% in September mainly because of higher petrol and diesel prices.
Inflation is at its highest rate in a year as energy prices have accelerated largely due to the US-Israel war with Iran.
In response to prices surging, the Bank of England raised interest rates for the first time in three years earlier this month, in a bid to slow inflation to its target of 2%.
Interest rates increased from 3.75% to 4%, and the Bank signalled a further rise could be likely unless the conflict in the Middle East is resolved.
Higher interest rates lift the cost of borrowing for some mortgages, loans and credit cards, but can also lead to a better return on savings.
Emma Reynolds, chief secretary to the Treasury, said the government was providing help for households with energy costs.
VAT has been cut on electricity bills to zero until next July and the government will also hand £100 to 20 million homes in January.
But with annual household energy bills forecast to reach £2,166, Cornwall Insight's retail markets principal, Craig Lowrey, said that "ultimately this support can only chip away at the edges of a bill that continues to be pushed up by events in the Middle East".
Sophie, who manages a cafe at the Old Boat Corner community centre in Brighton, told the BBC she watches her smart meter at home "like a hawk".
"I'm very conscious of the cost of energy, and it is having an impact on how we function in the home as a family," she said.
"I try to cook using the oven a lot less than I used to. We haven't got the heating on yet in our household. We're just like 'wear more layers'. We've got electric blankets on the sofa."
Shadow chancellor, Andrew Griffith, said four successive rises in the inflation rate was down to the UK's "soaring energy costs" and Labour's decision to "hike taxes and employment costs".
Grant Fitzner, chief economist at the ONS, said fuel prices were "once again a major contributor" to the increase in the inflation rate in October.
Rising energy prices can lead to more expensive food and staples for consumers if businesses pass on higher costs.
Earlier this month, the Bank of England said there had been "limited evidence" of this, with some firms absorbing cost increases and accepting lower profit margins.
But Fitzner said on Wednesday: "Annual costs of both raw materials and goods leaving factories continue to climb, driven by higher crude oil and petrol prices, respectively."
Petrol prices rose by 5.2p per litre between September and October, the ONS said, with the average price last month hitting 174.7p per litre - the highest since August 2022.
Diesel prices, meanwhile, reached the highest price since records began 30 years ago, averaging 199.5p per litre in October.
But the ONS said price inflation in restaurants and cafes had slowed last month, and that prices had fallen on average for hotels.
And food price inflation rose by 0.9%, the slowest pace in five years.
Core inflation, which strips out energy and food costs, and services inflation were little changed on last month. The figure is closely watched by the Bank of England when setting interest rates.
It could mean the Bank opts to hold off on a further rate rise in December, though policymakers believe inflation could peak at 4.9% in the middle of next year and not return to 2% until 2028.
In an "adverse scenario", where the US-Iran war could escalate further and send oil prices higher, inflation could reach 6.2% in 2027, it has suggested.
A spokesperson for the Bank said it decided to raise rates two weeks ago to "limit how much higher energy costs affect other prices, and will continue to set interest rates to make sure inflation returns to the 2% target and stays there".
Additional reporting by Raphael Sheridan, economics producer

Increase in October piles pressure on households as Iran war pushes up oil cost and rattles global economy
Energy bills in Great Britain forecast to rise by 26% to £2,166 from January
Inflation in the UK rose to 3.6% in October after petrol prices rose and diesel hit a record high amid the fallout from the war in the Middle East.
Figures from the Office for National Statistics show the headline rate of inflation as measured by the consumer prices index rose from 3.5% in September and was in line with City economists’ forecasts.
As households brace for the colder winter months with household gas and electricity costs soaring, the latest figures push the headline inflation rate to the highest level in a year.
Grant Fitzner, the ONS chief economist, said: “Inflation rose slightly in October, with fuel prices once again a major contributor to the increase in the annual rate.
“Annual costs of both raw materials and goods leaving factories continue to climb, driven by higher crude oil and petrol prices respectively.”
Fuel prices for motorists rose at an annual rate of 33.2%, the largest increase since July 2022 after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine sparked a global increase in energy prices.
The average price of petrol rose by 5.2p a litre between September and October to reach 174.7p a litre, the highest level in four years. Diesel prices rose by 7p a litre to 199.5p a litre, the highest price on records dating back to 1996.
Andy Burnham’s government has pledged to offer support for households grappling with a fresh cost of living squeeze as the stop-start Iran conflict rattles the global economy and drives up inflation worldwide.
At the budget last month the chancellor, John Healey, announced plans for a £100 winter handout for 20m households to cushion the blow from the global economic storm.
The latest inflation figures took into account a 4% increase in the Ofgem energy price cap from the start of October.
A new forecast from the consultancy Cornwall Insight on Wednesday predicted a 26% jump in energy bills in Great Britain from January to the equivalent of £2,166 a year for a typical household.
Economic forecasters predict a further rise in inflation, with the Bank of England anticipating a peak of close to 5% next year.
Earlier this month Threadneedle Street raised interest rates from 3.75% to 4% and warned further increases in the cost of borrowing might be required to combat inflationary pressures unleashed by the Iran war.
A spokesperson for the Bank said: “The conflict in the Middle East has caused energy prices and inflation to rise in recent months, and inflation is expected to rise further by the middle of next year due to cost pressures already in the pipeline.
“The MPC raised bank rate two weeks ago to limit how much higher energy costs affect other prices, and will continue to set interest rates to make sure inflation returns to the 2% target and stays there.”
Financial markets anticipate at least two quarter-point increases before the end of next year. Analysts said the Bank could be forced to raise borrowing costs from as early as next month.
Core inflation – which excludes volatile energy, food, alcohol and tobacco prices – was unchanged at 2.8%, matching economists’ forecasts. Services inflation, which the Bank has been monitoring closely for evidence of domestic inflationary pressures becoming entrenched, also held steady at 3.7%, slightly below City predictions for a rate of 3.8%.
Air fares rose by 1.8% between September and October amid an increase in long-haul ticket prices – offset by a downward effect from European flights. Prices for alcohol and tobacco also rose, by 4.5%, influenced by the timing of an increase in tobacco duty at the start of the month.
Food prices rose at the slowest rate since September 2021, at 0.9%, down from 1.3% in September.
Emma Reynolds, the chief secretary to the Treasury, said: “The conflict in the Middle East and Russia’s illegal invasion of Ukraine have pushed up costs around the world.
“The household energy payment, announced in our budget, is providing £100 directly into 20 million bank accounts in January, which will help to give families breathing space now.
“The budget also started the long-term action needed to get energy costs down for good, including an end to levies on household bills, scrapping standing charges and ensuring Britain is better protected from global shocks in the future.”

Public health leaders condemn ‘significant damage’ by Trump administration as calls grow for RFK Jr to resign
Doctors and public health leaders expressed grief and alarm at the loss of US measles-free status, a hard-won public health victory that once made the US a leader in infectious disease elimination.
Measles was declared resurgent in the United States, Bolivia and Mexico by the Pan American Health Organization (Paho) on Tuesday, meaning the virus has spread continuously for 12 months.
The announcement formally ends a 26-year record of measles elimination in the US, and comes amid the worst measles outbreak since 1991, making the loss of measles elimination status widely predicted. The Americas were once the only measles-free World Health Organization (WHO) region on the globe.
“There’s no question it was emotional, because we’ve been working on this initiative for decades,” Dr Jon Andrus, the chair of the Paho advisory committee that recommended the US lose its measles elimination status, told the Guardian.
“To see the US, once a global leader, lose its status is of course sad,” Andrus continued, citing the work of friends and colleagues, “and it was also sad to see our Mexican colleagues lose their status, as well as Bolivia.”
That grief was in sharp contrast to the reaction of the Trump administration. Health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, who has spent years spreading misinformation about the measles, mumps and rubella combination vaccine (MMR) and downplaying the disease, had his agency promote an appearance with a Texas-based chef and posted a picture of himself as James Bond this week. After devastating midterm losses, Trump appointed Maha advocate Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff.
Measles elimination status is a public health designation. It does not come with penalties or travel restrictions. Instead, it is a project of public health workers, from localities to international officials, who rank vaccination among the most cost-effective ways to improve human life, an intervention ranked alongside public sanitation and clean drinking water .
“There’s a huge return on investment that is pretty amazing,” said Andrus.
The loss of elimination status has already heightened calls for Kennedy to be fired – including from critical swing vote senators such as Republican Bill Cassidy of Louisiana. On Sunday , Cassidy called Kennedy’s tenure as health secretary “a series of failures”. Democratic senator of Georgia Raphael Warnock criticized Kennedy for posting “AI slop” when the US lost its measles-free status.
For his part, Kennedy said in a statement posted on X late on Tuesday afternoon that the US “will stop measles outbreaks, protect American families, and work to regain US measles elimination status”.
He added that he would “continue to recommend MMR vaccination as the most effective way to prevent measles” and that officials with the Department of Health and Human Services “are working to close vaccination gaps and rebuild public trust. We will answer families’ questions honestly about vaccine benefits and risks and work with trusted health care providers and community leaders to prevent measles, limit its spread, and support timely treatment.”
The US is in the midst of the worst measles outbreak in decades, with more than 5,400 cases and 10 measles-associated deaths reported by state health authorities. Measles is considered one of the most infectious diseases known to medicine. The infection kills one to three unvaccinated people per 1,000 and hospitalizes up to one in five.
“The measles virus is not harmless,” said American Academy of Pediatrics President Dr Andrew D Racine. “It can cause pneumonia, hospitalization, brain damage and death. We have an extraordinary tool to prevent it: a safe, effective, inexpensive, and readily available vaccine.”
Notably, the worst of this year’s outbreak would not have even been considered by Andrus and colleagues at Paho, since the group only examined data from the first half of 2026. The announcement was nevertheless widely predicted and even leaked. It comes amid a global resurgence in measles that saw Canada lose its measles-free status in 2025, and the UK this year.
“As a pediatrician and a parent, I am heartbroken that we have reached this point,” Dr Richard Besser, president and CEO of the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation, and a former acting director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), said in a statement.
“Medical providers and state, local, and tribal health officials across America are doing what they can to stop current measles outbreaks and prevent new ones,” said Besser. “Yet for the past two years, the federal government has largely been missing in action. That needs to change. It is no surprise that the resurgence of measles has coincided with an administration that has inflicted significant damage to our healthcare system while spreading false claims about vaccines.”
Democratic senator-elect Dr Annie Andrews of South Carolina, a critic of Kennedy and one of several newly elected doctors and scientists , told the Guardian: “We need to restore trust in public health, make sure every family has access to life-saving vaccines, and put the health and safety of our children ahead of our politics.”
Health experts also called on the US to begin work on an action plan for Paho, one that could help the US stop transmission and make gains in vaccination. Considered a multi-year project, Brazil lost measles-free status in 2019 and regained it five years later. On Tuesday, Paho announced that Canada had stopped transmission for 60 days, a step toward regaining its measles-free status.
As measles spreads in the US, Americans face a new reality where pockets of low vaccination rates can combust into outbreaks. In places such as Cleveland, Ohio, a nearby outbreak has spurred the local public health director to tell residents to find decades-old vaccination certificates, lest they be exposed and require a blood draw or quarantine.
“Because measles is so contagious, it’s considered a bellwether, a signal of problems in efforts to control disease,” epidemiologist Gregg Gonsalves, a Yale researcher who serves on the coordinating committee for advocacy group Defend Public Health, said in a statement.
“RFK Jr has spent over a decade trying to destroy disease prevention, the last two as HHS secretary, and his public health malpractice is coming home to roost.
