Peltola’s Alaska win gives Democrats 56 Senate seats and a buffer in Republican states ahead of the 2028 elections.
Democrat Mary Peltola has won the United States Senate seat in Alaska, unseating two-term Republican Senator Dan Sullivan. It is the Democrats’ first US Senate win in the state in more than a decade.
As of early Wednesday, The Associated Press news agency’s count gave her 50.1 percent of first-choice votes against Sullivan’s 45.8 percent, with an estimated 99 percent of votes counted.
Clearing the 50 percent mark matters. Alaska uses ranked-choice voting, so a candidate who wins a majority of first-choice votes is elected outright, with no further rounds of counting.
The vote has been closely watched, not just because it is the last Senate race to be called in the midterm elections, but because of a Republican legal challenge to the election over the listing of two candidates with nearly the same name – Republican Dan Sullivan and independent Daniel Sullivan. The legal challenge was thrown out just days before the election.
The Trump administration alleged that Peltola’s campaign had deliberately recruited the second Dan Sullivan to divide Republican votes in the state – a practice known as “ ballot stacking “.
But on Tuesday, it was clear that even if the “official” Dan Sullivan had received all the votes of his namesake, he would not have gained enough to beat Peltola.
Peltola’s win brings Democratic control of the Senate to 56 seats, against the Republicans’ 44.
Peltola, a Yup’ik Alaskan, became the first Alaska Native to be elected to Congress when she won a special election for the state’s sole House of Representatives seat in 2022. She served from September 2022 to January 2025, losing her re-election bid in 2024.
On the Senate campaign trail this year, she played down her Democratic label, which remains unpopular in the state, and focused on local issues such as energy jobs, border security and gun rights.
Scott Lucas, a professor of international politics at University College Dublin’s Clinton Institute, told Al Jazeera that Peltola is viewed as a “safe pair of hands”.
“Alaska is a very small population, with a very, very large landmass, so it’s very important that you try to build up, across that large landmass, ties and community ties,” he said. “Peltola was seen as someone who had represented Alaska’s interests very well.”
Lucas described her as “a pragmatist, very much in that centre line of Democratic politics”. “Not too provocative, doesn’t really play identity politics,” he said. “She didn’t play on the idea this is all about Native Americans, even though she happens to be a Native American.”
Sullivan, by contrast, “was tarnished because he was there on Trump’s ticket, as it were”, Lucas said, though “he was very much a local candidate”. “Had the Trump administration done a better job on the issues, then I suspect Sullivan holds his seat,” he added.
In late May, Dan J Sullivan, a retired teacher from Petersburg, entered the race. On June 15, the state elections division removed him from the ballot. It said he had chosen the name to cause confusion with the senator, and pointed to his use of a political consultant who had previously worked for Peltola.
The courts reversed that decision. A superior court judge ruled he was eligible, and the Alaska Supreme Court upheld that ruling on June 29. The two candidates appeared on the ballot as “Daniel J Sullivan Jr”, with no party affiliation, and “Dan S Sullivan”, Republican and incumbent. The retired teacher finished in the top four of the August primary, earning a place on the November ballot.
Republicans claimed he was a decoy. The New York Times later reported that Peltola campaign staff and Democratic operatives had worked to get him to contest. At Trump’s urging, the Department of Justice (DoJ) sued to delay certification if Senator Sullivan lost and to separate ballots cast for his namesake. Federal Judge Sharon Gleason dismissed the case on November 1. The DoJ said it would appeal.
Lucas said this kind of “ballot stacking” – backing a minor candidate to pull votes from a rival – is not uncommon, and both parties have engaged in it in the past. If the second Sullivan had taken 2 percent of the vote, he explained, he could have pushed the incumbent below the 50 percent mark and forced a ranked-choice count. “You drain enough support from the Republican that you give yourself a better chance of winning,” he said.
In the end, he said, “I don’t think it made that much of a difference.” AP’s count gave Daniel J Sullivan Jr 1.7 percent, and Peltola won more than 50 percent of the vote.
Peltola is the first Democrat to represent Alaska in the Senate since Sullivan unseated Mark Begich in 2014. Her win is not a deciding factor in which party controls the chamber – Democrats already had enough seats to control the Senate – but Lucas said it is “significant in a wider context”.
Alaska is the latest in a string of Republican strongholds to switch to Democrats.
On election night, Democrats flipped seats in North Carolina, South Carolina, Ohio, Texas, Kansas, Iowa and Maine. Later-arriving counts then confirmed that Mississippi had flipped, electing its first Black senator in 150 years, and now Alaska has taken the tally to nine.
Texas went Democratic for the first time since 1988, and Kansas for the first time since 1932.
“Alaska was one of the seats that it was thought that the Democrats might win,” Lucas said. “So that in itself is not as surprising as, say, Mississippi, which is really, really surprising. South Carolina was quite a surprise as well. But still, it reaffirms the extent of this Democratic surge.”
Those wins also give Democrats a buffer. Senators serve six-year terms, with about one-third of the 100 seats contested every two years, so the seats won this month will not be on the ballot again until 2032. By holding seats in states they would not normally carry, Democrats can make it much harder for Republicans to retake the Senate in 2028.
Finally, the win brings Democrats closer to the magical two-thirds majority. They now hold 56 seats, which Lucas called “a pretty good majority when even the most optimistic analysts regarding the Democrats were looking at 53 seats at most”. They will still need Republican support on issues to secure the two-thirds majority needed to overturn a presidential veto in both chambers.
A two-thirds vote in the Senate is needed to convict an official in an impeachment trial. The more seats Democrats hold, the fewer Republicans they need to win over to reach that threshold. For now, Lucas said, “They cannot pass legislation because Trump can veto it. So they still have to try to work with Republicans if they want to get any legislation across.”
Lucas expects the new Democratic majorities to propose legislation and hold hearings on accountability, “whether that be with respect to AI and technology, whether it be with respect to the Epstein case”, or the wealth of Trump and his family, including through cryptocurrency. “Meanwhile, the Republicans are a fractured party,” he said.
In North Carolina, South Carolina and Texas, Trump’s inner circle imposed candidates on the party, and all three were lost. Democrats, by contrast, “went for more organic candidates, and Mary Peltola was one of them”, Lucas said.
“Diversity has become a bad word with the Trump camp,” Lucas said. “It’s interesting that in this very diverse election, you have your first US Muslim senator, you have your first US openly gay man in the Senate, and you have two Native American women who have won: Peggy Flanagan in Minnesota, and then Peltola. In this case, it was the party with the diversity of candidates that did better.”

Knesset’s appointment of Matan Kahana marks step towards reversing policies of outgoing government
The Israeli parliament elected a new speaker on Tuesday, a key step toward rolling back policies passed by the outgoing government led by the prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu .
The new speaker is Matan Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot , the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace Netanyahu .
Eisenkot’s bloc has pledged to undo some of Netanyahu’s most contentious policies following Kahana’s election.
He was approved as speaker with 66 votes in the 120-member chamber, backed by the Jewish-led opposition parties and by the Arab-led parties. The candidate backed by Netanyahu’s bloc, Ofir Katz, received 52 votes following a stormy debate that stretched over seven hours.
“The appointment of Matan Kahana as Knesset speaker is a worthy democratic move that reflects the absolute majority in favour of change,” Eisenkot said ahead of the vote.
The vote took place weeks after the parliamentary elections on 27 October in which Netanyahu and his allies lost their parliamentary majority. Eisenkot was subsequently tasked by Israel’s president with trying to form a new coalition government.
Eisenkot has up to five more weeks to secure enough alliances to form a coalition.
As negotiations continue on the sidelines, his bloc, along with unaffiliated Arab-led parties, can use their majority in the newly sworn-in Knesset to advance their legislative agenda.
They introduced several bills last week, including to set term limits on the role of prime minister, to form a government-led inquiry into the Hamas-led 7 October 2023 attacks and to reverse laws that limit the powers of the judiciary.
Kahana gives the opposition bloc a major legislative advantage, according to Assaf Shapira of the Israel Democracy Institute, a Jerusalem thinktank.
“It’s important because there is not much time, because the speaker of the Knesset can make the legislative process much, much faster or much slower,” Shapira said.
Eisenkot and his allies are under pressure to swiftly advance their legislative priorities in the weeks ahead. Roy Folkman, a member of Eisenkot’s Yashar party, heads the temporary committee that decides much of the Knesset’s work until a government is formed.
If Eisenkot fails to form a government, the Israeli president could give Netanyahu an opportunity to do so. That would probably give Netanyahu’s Likud party control of the committee.
Even though Netanyahu’s opponents would still hold a majority, they would “feel that their momentum has gone”, Shapira said, and there would be a “real danger that some of the legislation will be delayed”.
Chamber procedures will pose a further challenge. A bill has to be introduced on the floor, considered in committee and voted on several times on the floor before it passes the Knesset. That winding process could make it hard to move bills across the finish line before time runs out.
Shapira said Eisenkot and his allies are likely to prioritise rolling back controversial laws that gave the government a larger role in appointing judges and weakened the power of Israel’s attorney general, an independent role that is seen by many as central to Israel’s system of government checks and balances.
“It’s very easy to abolish these laws because no new institution has to be created,” he said.
Establishing a body to investigate the 7 October attacks would be easier, Shapira added, and carry greater legitimacy once a government is formed.
Netanyahu’s opponents argue he has blocked an independent probe into any military or intelligence failures around the day, the deadliest in Israel’s history, and evaded accountability.

A senior US defence official has criticised Ukraine's "deep strikes" against Russia, saying they had been ineffective in bringing the war to an end and arguing that, in some cases, they had likely "hardened the Russian public's resolve."
"Our assessment is that such strikes have not been effective in driving an end to the war, nor do they contribute to blunting Russia's advances on the front line," Under Secretary of Defence Elbridge Colby said while speaking from NATO's headquarters in Brussels on Tuesday.
"Such strikes, especially those that target civilian infrastructure such as Wildberries, have actually probably hardened the Russian public's resolve and the Kremlin's own willingness to escalate," he continued.
He added that support for Kyiv moving forward should focus on "enabling and advancing Ukraine's ability to hold the line of battle and where possible make gains."
Ukraine has increasingly struck targets deep inside Russian territory as the war has gone on, using its burgeoning drone technology to carry out long-range attacks.
Ukrainian forces have particularly looked to target energy infrastructure such as oil refineries and terminals, as well as military sites like air bases, as they have sought to hamper the Russian economy and hit Vladimir Putin's war machine.
US President Donald Trump has previously demanded that Ukraine halt strikes on Russian oil refineries, saying the attacks were to blame for rising diesel fuel prices.
Colby's comments have drawn pushback from some European officials.
German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius called the warning "quite a stupid thing," while his British counterpart Wes Streeting said there was "no doubt" in his mind that Ukraine's long-range strikes had "helped to degrade Putin's war machine, buying time and saving lives."
The comments came as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy once again urged allies to speed up deliveries of interceptor missiles.
"Ukraine needs Patriot and IRIS-T interceptors from the stocks you already have right now," he told the meeting of the Ukraine Defence Contact Group in Brussels via video link.
"And I ask the United States – please, do not delay these deliveries," Zelenskyy added. He also said Ukraine needed a further 40 F-16 fighter jets to help boost its air defences.
The pleas come as Ukraine gears up for what looks set to be another brutal winter under heavy bombardment from Russian forces.
Russia has repeatedly sought to ramp up attacks on Ukraine in wartime winter periods, targeting the country's energy sector as Moscow has attempted to break its resolve.

Files show Epstein-linked payments at $582m, far more than previously known, and tie Trump business dealings to suspected money laundering networks.
A leak of more than 15 million internal records from Deutsche Bank has shed new light on its dealings with United States President Donald Trump, the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and other powerful figures.
The Inside Deutsche Bank investigation, published on Tuesday by a consortium of international news outlets, has put Germany’s biggest bank back in the spotlight after years of trying to rebuild its reputation following its failures to prevent money laundering.
Files containing millions of emails, minutes of meetings and internal reports were leaked by two whistleblowers whose identities and links to the institution have been withheld for their protection, according to Le Monde, one of the participating news outlets. The pair told the media groups they believed the bank was engaging in criminal activity and that releasing the documents was in the public interest.
An Indian journalist and a South African journalist obtained the cache, then shared it with more than 230 reporters from about 50 news organisations, including Der Spiegel, the Financial Times and The New York Times, in an internationally coordinated effort.
The material includes some nine million emails, as well as meeting minutes, due diligence reports and financial crime reports dating back to the early 2010s, many of them from the bank’s internal investigations.
The whistleblowers also passed the data to US prosecutors and financial crime authorities, and could be eligible for a reward if Washington prosecutes the bank based on their leaks. Le Monde said the whistleblowers were not paid by the journalists and placed no conditions on how the material was used.
Deutsche Bank said concerns raised by the investigation “date back many years” and that it had since strengthened its controls, adding that it did not expect any meaningful financial impact. The bank’s chairman reaffirmed the board’s support for chief executive Christian Sewing, who has run the institution since 2018.
“Deutsche Bank is a different bank today,” the bank said in a statement.
The files identify more than $3m in transactions involving Trump-owned companies, including payments linked to suspected Russian and Azerbaijani money-laundering networks.
Deutsche Bank extended loans to Trump for years, even after a string of bankruptcies and defaults at his businesses from the early 1990s. By January 2021, it was his biggest creditor, with about $340m in loans to his company outstanding.
That month, following the January 6 assault on the US Capitol by protesters wanting to stop the certification of Democrat Joe Biden’s win in the presidential election, the bank ceased doing business with him, according to The New York Times. Trump had claimed the election had been rigged against him, of which there has never been any proof.
The Financial Times reported that the bank inadvertently sent a Trump tax document to another client’s accountant in 2017, during his first term in office, and never told him about the error. Asked about the disclosure during his visit to Manila for the ASEAN summit on Tuesday, Trump said the bank should not have released that information.
“They shouldn’t have done it. It’s illegal for them to do it,” he said. Deutsche Bank declined to comment on his remarks.
The leaked records also reveal special monitoring that the bank applied to Trump’s accounts, and its handling of them has drawn scrutiny before.
In 2019, The New York Times reported that Deutsche Bank had failed to alert US authorities to suspicious transactions linked to Trump. The bank said at the time that none of its investigators had been prevented from escalating such concerns.
The leaked files list about $582m in transactions linked to Epstein, which were flagged internally as suspicious. That is more than double the amount previously identified as being overlooked or not reported by banks during US Senate investigations . When the Senate findings were released in August, a Deutsche Bank spokesperson said the bank regretted its “historical connection” with Epstein.
Epstein, who was a US financier, became a Deutsche Bank client in 2013, five years after pleading guilty in Florida to procuring a minor for prostitution, and remained a client until 2018. He died in a New York jail in 2019 while awaiting trial on sex trafficking charges.
Internal emails in the newly leaked cache indicate that senior executives approved Epstein as a client despite his conviction, and kept his accounts open even after warnings about the activities of Ghislaine Maxwell, his former girlfriend and associate. Maxwell was convicted in 2021 of helping Epstein sexually abuse teenage girls. She is currently serving a 20-year prison sentence.
The files also reveal information about payments linked to wealthy Epstein associates such as private equity billionaire Leon Black and Wall Street financier Glenn Dubin.
A review commissioned by Black’s firm previously found he had paid Epstein $158m between 2012 and 2017 for tax and estate planning advice. Black has sought to distance himself from Epstein, repeatedly denying wrongdoing or any knowledge of his abuse of girls and young women.
The leak comes years after the bank paid fines and settlements of more than $200m over its handling of Epstein-related finances. In 2020, regulators fined it $150m for compliance failures linked to Epstein and other high-risk clients, finding that he had held more than 40 accounts at the bank. In 2023, it agreed to pay $75m to settle a suit brought by women who alleged they had been abused by him.
The documents also detail Deutsche Bank’s business dealings in Russia up until Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, despite concerns raised by some managers.
They include previously undisclosed internal warnings about the bank’s continued dealings with wealthy Kremlin-connected clients despite sanctions and money laundering concerns.
Those named include Russian billionaires Roman Abramovich, the former owner of English football club Chelsea, and aluminium tycoon Oleg Deripaska. Both men were sanctioned by the United Kingdom in 2022. Suleiman Kerimov, another billionaire whose name appears in the files, was sanctioned by the US in 2014 and 2018.
Transactions associated with Rifaat al-Assad , the uncle of former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad, also appear in the files. Rifaat, who died in January, was convicted in France in 2020 of acquiring millions of euros’ worth of property with funds diverted from the Syrian state.
Other files concern figures connected to the Sarkozy-Libya affair, in which former French President Nicolas Sarkozy was convicted in 2025 of criminal conspiracy over efforts to secure funding for his 2007 campaign from the government of late Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi.

Police in the Philippines have asked prosecutors to charge Thomas Markle Sr, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, with possession of and intent to distribute child sexual abuse material.
Cebu province prosecutor Graeme Elmido told the BBC that police had filed documents requesting that Markle be charged on Monday.
Earlier this month, Markle, 82, was separately arrested and charged in the US with possession of child sexual abuse material. The FBI said agents seized about 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books that they allege contained child sex abuse material, from storage units Markle rented.
Markle, who is in custody in the US, has previously denied the allegations. The BBC has contacted Markle's attorney for comment.
Elmido told the BBC that Philippine National Police had asked prosecutors to charge Markle with "two counts of intent to distribute CSAEM [child sexual abuse and exploitation material], and one count of possession of CSAEM material".
Last month, police in the Philippines obtained a warrant to examine devices allegedly removed from Markle's former home in the country.
Four boxes of material, including computers, phones, hard drives and old video tapes, were handed to officers by Meghan's half brother Thomas Markle Jr.
Earlier this month, Markle Sr was arrested and charged in the US. He had initially been placed under house detention at his assisted living facility in Florida, but was taken back into custody last week after prosecutors alleged he removed his ankle monitor.
Meghan Markle has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year, telling him she and the authorities knew he had abused young girls.
In a previously shared statement after the allegations against her father emerged, Meghan wrote: "I am deeply distressed... my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."
She said she hoped it could be understood why she had largely cut off contact from her father and did "not allow him to have contact with our children".
Correction 18 November: An earlier version of this story said that police in the Philippines have charged Thomas Markle Sr with possession of and intent to distribute child sexual abuse material. The story has been updated to clarify that police have asked prosecutors to charge him with possession of and intent to distribute child sexual abuse material.

Haiti announced on Tuesday that it formalised a "cooperation agreement" with El Salvador, the same day thousands of Haitians showed support in the streets of Port-au-Prince for soldiers sent by President Nayib Bukele to confront armed gangs in the capital.
"The Council of Ministers has approved the Cooperation agreement between the Republic of Haiti and the Republic of El Salvador," according to a Facebook post from the Haitian executive, who called it "a new stage in strengthening bilateral relations and cooperation."
Signs carried by the demonstrators on Tuesday read "Thank you, Bukele," and "Long live Bukele," according to photographs taken by an AFP journalist.
"Bukele, the country belongs to you! Do whatever you want with it," some chanted in the streets of a capital long subsumed by gang violence that has seized control of large sections.
Bukele has sent more than 2,000 troops to Haiti since late October, after four soldiers from his country went missing during an operation of the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF).
The new Salvadoran deployment, despite being separate from the GSF, has been welcomed by Haitian authorities, who have long sought reinforcements.
"We are asking President Bukele to ignore the detractors and to continue supporting Haiti," a demonstrator who declined to be identified for security reasons told AFP.
Numerous armed forces are now operating in Haiti, with uncertain levels of coordination, including the Haitian police and army, the multinational GSF, foreign mercenaries and most recently, the Salvadoran soldiers.
Bukele, whose forceful gang crackdown at home has won public support but sparked accusations of rights violations, appears prepared for more than just finding the four lost soldiers.
On 10 November, he boasted of having destroyed the "headquarters" of one of Haiti's main gangs, accompanied by video footage of the helicopter attack.
Since then, Bukele's forces have taken over a football stadium in the capital with the support of Haiti's national police.
On Tuesday, the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights called on all security forces to protect the population and resort to lethal force only as a last resort.
In the first 10 months of 2026, the UN recorded 4,595 deaths and 2,050 injuries to armed violence in Haiti.
In Miami over the weekend, at a football match between Haiti and the United States, some Haitian fans cheered on both their national team and Bukele, expressing high hopes the island's gangs can be contained.
Despite the 6-0 loss to the US in the Concacaf Nations League match, Haitians expressed optimism, waving Salvadoran flags and shouting "Bukele! Bukele!"
"All I can say is 'Viva Bukele!'," said 41-year-old Haitian fan Guito Ledix, adding that Bukele "is the only one trying to see if there's any possibility of getting rid of the gangs."
Haiti, the poorest country in the Americas, has faced a deep political and security crisis for years, with gangs seizing control of the island nation through a campaign of violence marked by murder, kidnapping and rape.
From Miami, home to one of the largest concentrations of Haitian immigrants, 28-year-old Stephanie Jeanty frets about the safety of her family still living there.
"Before I was a bit more stressed, but now, seeing the Salvadoran delegation that is working to restore peace, it's something, things are better," she said.
"I would really like to go back to my country. For now, no."

A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza
Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay , if the court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide against the Rohingya.
The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.
Lawyers representing Rohingya survivors say patterns of behaviour by Myanmar’s military, including killing people as they fled, show clear attempts to destroy the group during assaults on Rakhine state in 2016 and 2017.
It is the role of independent judges to interpret the genocide convention. However, judges at the court have taken advice on how to protect their assets from potential US sanctions, as a genocide ruling could be interpreted by Washington as lowering the “legal threshold” for the crime.
The Foundation for Defense of Democracies, an influential thinktank close to the White House, has predicted a genocide ruling will lead to the US imposing sanctions on the ICJ.
The US and Israel fear the final judgment may clarify how to establish a government’s intent to commit a genocide, and so set a precedent that makes it more likely the court will later rule that Israel committed genocide in Gaza.
Myanmar, which has denied carrying out a genocide, claims its actions targeted a military uprising by insurgents.
The ICJ, sometimes described as the UN’s top court, is responsible for settling interstate disputes, unlike the international criminal court (ICC), which prosecutes individuals accused of war crimes and other international crimes.
The US has already imposed crippling sanctions on judges at the ICC after the court issued arrest warrants against the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu. The US has also announced sanctions against the entire ICC as an institution, which it described as a “rogue court”. Washington fears the ICC could go after US troops.
The Gambia, as a litigant, was entitled to appoint an ad hoc judge in the case against Myanmar and chose the South African lawyer Pillay, who in October was awarded the Nobel peace prize . She is required to act as a jurist and not an advocate for the Gambia.
Mike Waltz, the US ambassador to the UN, has sent a warning shot to Pillay and the 15 ICJ judges, saying Washington “will not allow globalist, faux judges to weaponise the law against our troops”.
Waltz asserted last month: “The ICJ ad hoc judge Navi Pillay is tipping the scales on the ICJ’s current proceedings on Myanmar, intending to lower the legal threshold for proving genocide so that weakened and false standard can later be weaponised against American and allied soldiers whenever they raise a finger against terrorists that hide behind civilians.”
In remarks addressed to Pillay, he said: “We see your agenda and we’ll be watching the ICJ’s handling of these proceedings very closely.”
In a speech last Friday, the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio , said: “For this global elite, international law … is an instrument to advance their interests under the pretence of universal principles.”
He warned the ICC against quoting laws to “men with swords”.
Israel has previously criticised adverse advisory opinions issued by the ICJ and refused to implement 2024 orders requiring Israel to admit more aid into Gaza , and to cooperate with Unrwa, the UN relief and works agency.
In the Myanmar case, a 24-page submission jointly filed by the UK and five other mainly European states, argued that the ICJ, in judging intent to commit genocide, should examine a range of “facts and circumstances” assessed “comprehensively and holistically”.
It also stressed that genocide was not solely defined by killings, and that the treatment of children, gender-based violence and forced displacement were also relevant.
The US until recently had taken a relatively more benign view of The Hague-based ICJ, and under Antony Blinken as US secretary of state determined that Myanmar had committed genocide.
The 15 ICJ judges are elected for nine-year terms by the UN security council and the UN general assembly.
Rubio has given the ICC until April to respond to his criticisms before he imposes sanctions.
On Friday, the ICC formally decided to drop plans to prosecute US soldiers and intelligence agents for potentially unlawful acts in Afghanistan. The shelving of the near-dormant inquiry came after it was agreed evidence would be hard to obtain, but one side-effect may be a greater willingness on the part of the US to abandon its plan to impose sanctions on the ICC.

PRESS REVIEW – Wednesday, November 18: A joint investigation following the leak of 15 million documents shows that Deutsche Bank turned a blind eye to the criminal activities of some of its clients. Next, for its 175th birthday, The New York Times has chosen the top 10 stories that made history. Wired is focusing on the moments that defined 2026. Finally, we bring you a story about American parents whose children dream of becoming Formula 1 drivers. But how much does that dream cost?
The Financial Times reports that in 2018, when CEO Christian Sewing took over at Deutsche Bank, he promised to put an end to scandals and clean up the bank. Eight years later, the reality is quite different. The British daily investigated the leak of 15 million documents in collaboration with several international media outlets, including Le Monde and Der Spiegel . The Financial Times says the documents expose "bad behaviour, systemic failures, incompetence and broken promises". The leak and the reporting throw a new light on the career of the chief executive and his double standards. Der Spiegel writes about Deutsche Bank's "dark secrets". It points out that when Sewing took over, the institution had already been accused of various shortcomings, including money laundering . The bank had already been the subject of at least 27 raids and had received fines and sanctions totalling more than €20 billion since the beginning of the 2000s.
The bank is also under fire for its ties to Russian oligarchs and convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein . Der Spiegel specifically names several Russian oligarchs subject to sanctions, as well as Epstein. The German magazine reports that the late paedophile became a client of Deutsche Bank in 2013 – well after his conviction in 2008 – a conviction which Deutsche Bank was fully aware of. The sexual predator carried out his transactions there, totalling more than half a billion dollars, until 2019. The bank finally stopped working with Epstein three days after his arrest. Le Monde looks at the bank's links with another famous – or infamous – American: US President Donald Trump . An internal investigation established "a formal and direct link" between at least one of Trump's companies and money-laundering operations in Azerbaijan . Deutsche Bank knew this but didn't sever its ties with the US president – it just reinforced confidentiality, protecting both Trump and itself.
Next, it's The New York Times 's 175th birthday. For the occasion, the paper has chosen the 10 days that changed the world since the paper started publishing. For example, "The Day God Was Dethroned" – on November 24, 1859, Charles Darwin published "On the Origin of Species" and changed how people see their place in the universe; "The Day We Saw Our End" – on August 6, 1945, the United States bombed Hiroshima with the atomic bomb; and "The Day That Rewired Us" – on October 29, 1969, the first message on the ARPANET network was sent, the ancestor of the internet as we know it today.
Wired Magazine is focusing on 2026 in its "inaugural yearbook". It celebrates the people, inventions and viral moments that defined this year. For example, Jensen Huang is in the "most striking exit" category, winning "for the greatest reversal of fortune this year". The Strait of Hormuz is in the "most contested" category, winning for "keeping tensions – and gas prices – incredibly high".
Finally, The Wall Street Journal reports that "parents are spending fortunes to turn six-year-olds into F1 drivers". They sign them up for expensive karting lessons, with facilities reporting record reservations. A training club membership costs hundreds of thousands of dollars, but these are on the rise as well. Many parents are willing to pay the price, hoping their kid will be the next Formula 1 star.

Senegal were stripped of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title by a Confederation of African Football appeals board, and are awaiting the outcome of their own appeal at the Court of Arbitration for Sport
Senegal became the first side to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations before Cameroon and Morocco were among five others to join them with two games to spare - but there was penalty drama in Tripoli.
Tunisia, who have appeared at a record 17 consecutive editions of Afcon, are at risk of missing out after a contentious 1-1 draw against Libya.
Libya's penalty equaliser just before half-time followed protest scenes lasting over five minutes as players and staff from the Carthage Eagles challenged the decision.
The video assistant referee system is not used in Afcon qualifying, and Tunisia's remonstrating with the fourth official on the touchline ultimately only served to delay the spot-kick, which Ezoo El Mariamy, the player who was adjudged to have been fouled, converted.
Drawing the game meant Tunisia's winless start in Group H continued, with the Carthage Eagles having just three points from four games.
Tunisia need a strong finish to their campaign to give themselves a chance of reaching the finals, and Nigeria are also at risk of missing out, but others have made short order of qualifying.
Led by new head coach Patrick Vieira, Senegal moved to the brink of a place at the finals by beating Sudan 4-2 on Monday, and the Teranga Lions had their passage from Group J confirmed on Tuesday when Mozambique secured a 1-0 victory away against Ethiopia.
Cameroon and Benin also progressed without kicking a ball after Comoros and Burkina Faso registered wins - with the latter result also sealing a finals spot for the victorious Stallions.
Mali and Morocco extended their perfect starts and booked their places with triumphs over Rwanda and Niger respectively.
Abdellah Ouazane was the match-winner for Morocco in an away game that was actually played in Rabat, with the 17-year-old brilliantly curling in midway through the first half to cap a fine team move.
The Atlas Lions and Senegal are still waiting for the outcome of a case at the Court of Arbitration for Sport to decide the destination of the 2025 Afcon title.
Senegal won the final 1-0 after extra time but Morocco were awarded the trophy by a Confederation of African Football appeals board which decreed the West Africans breached competition regulations by leaving the field of play in second-half stoppage time in protest at a penalty awarded against them.
Cameroon, Senegal and Benin close in on Afcon 2027 qualification
Eleven sides had the chance to join co-hosts Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda at next year's finals when the fourth round of fixtures culminated on Tuesday.
Algeria, DR Congo, Egypt and the Ivorians all could have qualified with away wins but failed to pick up three points.
Brighton forward Yankuba Minteh was on target as The Gambia came from behind to lead Ivory Coast 2-1 in Group C, but Christ Inao Oulai grabbed an equaliser deep in stoppage time after Scorpions striker Muhammed Badamosi was sent off in the 90th minute.
Egypt were held to a goalless draw in Malawi, Sierra Leone claimed a late point against the Congolese and Algeria suffered a 3-0 defeat in Togo.
Angola beat South Sudan 1-0 in Juba and would have qualified had Egypt claimed victory in the other match in Group B.
Nigeria are in danger of failing to reach Afcon for the first time since 2017 after the Super Eagles failed to beat Tanzania.
The final two rounds of qualifiers will be held in March next year, with Afcon 2027 scheduled to be held in East Africa from 19 June to 17 July.
Malawi goalkeeper George Chikooka helped deny Mohamed Salah's Egypt an early passage to the Afcon 2027 finals in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda
Seven-time Afcon winners Egypt knew victory in Lilongwe could take them to the finals but were frustrated by an inspired second-half showing from Malawi goalkeeper George Chikooka.
After Pharaohs captain Mohamed Salah had hit the outside of the post from a tight angle, Chikooka denied Trezeguet and Haissem Hassan before also making fine stops from Mohamed Hany and Ibrahim Adel in stoppage time.
Egypt move on to eight points in Group B, two points behind Angola after Miro's first-half effort secured a 1-0 victory for the Palancas Negras in Juba.
There was drama as Ivory Coast salvaged a draw in Bakau through Inao Oulai's 98th-minute goal, which denied The Gambia a third win in Group C.
The Ivorians lead the pool on 10 points, with The Gambia on seven and Ghana on six following the Black Stars' back-to-back wins over Somalia.
DR Congo appeared on track to progress from Group E as Junior Kadile gave the Leopards a half-time lead in their away tie against Sierra Leone, but Alie Conteh netted in the 94th minute for the West Africans.
And Togo moved a point behind Group I leaders Algeria after a strong first-half showing in Lome, with two goals from Thibault Klidje before Kennedy Boateng's powerful header secured a 3-0 win over the 2019 champions from North Africa.
Eric Chelle's Nigeria failed to qualify for the 2026 Fifa World Cup and now face an uphill battle to reach Afcon 2027
Nigeria's hopes of progressing suffered another blow as Eric Chelle's men drew 0-0 with Tanzania in Zanzibar.
With East Africans Tanzania already assured of a spot at the finals, as co-hosts, Nigeria are competing with Guinea-Bissau for just one qualification spot available in Group L.
And Guinea-Bissau established a three-point advantage over the Super Eagles as goals from Mama Balde and Mauro Rodrigues gave them a 2-0 home win over Madagascar.
After falling to a 3-0 defeat in Bissau in September, even maximum points in the final two rounds of qualifiers may not be enough for three-time continental champions Nigeria to reach the tournament.
In another section with just one qualifying berth, Tunisia are in trouble at the foot of Group H on three points after the 1-1 draw with Libya in Tripoli.
Anis Ben Slimane capitalised on a defensive error to fire Tunisia ahead in the third minute, but El Mariamy levelled for the hosts from 12 yards in first-half injury time.
Tunisia's players and officials vehemently protested against the decision to award a foul after El Mariamy tussled with defender Ghaith Zaalouni and collided with goalkeeper Aymen Dahmen, delaying the penalty for several minutes.
The Tunisian visitors then had their own claims for a spot-kick turned down after a similar coming together between Mohamed Belhadj Mahmoud and Libya keeper Ayman Al Tihar, with players surrounding Beninois referee Adissa Ligali and his assistants at the full-time whistle.
The Carthage Eagles had also complained about refereeing decisions in the reverse fixture on Friday with a potential equaliser ruled out following a marginal offside call, before their North African neighbours sealed a 2-0 win.
Libya are one point behind Group H leaders Uganda after the Cranes drew 1-1 away against Botswana , who are one point better off than Tunisia.
Elsewhere, South Africa returned to the top of Group D with a 2-1 win over co-hosts Kenya , Cape Verde's chances of reaching the finals were hit by a 2-0 defeat in Liberia and Gabon suffered a shock 2-0 loss at the hands of Lesotho.

Pınar Altuğ'un Bebek 'teki Boğaz manzaralı dairesi, yıllardır magazin gündeminin eksik olmayan konularından biri. Ocak ayında dairenin satıldığı yazılmış, Altuğ ise bu iddiayı yalanlamıştı. Aradan geçen aylar sonra Sabah gazetesinden Bülent Cankurt'un köşesinde yeni bir satış iddiası yer aldı ve konu bir kez daha konuşulmaya başlandı.
Miss Turkey 1994 seçilerek adını duyuran Pınar Altuğ, modellikten oyunculuğa geçtikten sonra Çocuklar Duymasın dizisindeki Meltem karakteriyle ekran başındaki herkesin yakından tanıdığı bir isim oldu. İlk Aşkım dizisinde rol arkadaşı olan Yağmur Atacan'la 2008'de evlenen oyuncunun kızı Su ise ailenin en çok konuşulan isimlerinden biri haline geldi. Son yıllarda ekranlardan uzak kalsa da paylaşımlarıyla ve Su'nun Londra'daki üniversite macerasıyla gündemden düşmeyen Altuğ'un adı, bu kez Bebek 'teki dairesinin akıbetiyle anılıyor.
Sabah'taki köşe yazısında Bülent Cankurt, Pınar Altuğ'un Bebek 'te ünlü bir mekânın üst katında bulunan Boğaz manzaralı dairesini sattığını ve bedelin 85 milyon lira olduğunu yazdı. Güncel kurla yaklaşık 1,7 milyon dolara denk gelen bu rakam, ocak ayında dolaşıma giren 2,5 milyon dolarlık satış iddiasının ardından ortaya atıldı. Cankurt, Altuğ'un o iddiayı yalanladığını hatırlatırken bu kez oyuncunun evini gerçekten elden çıkardığını öne sürüyor. Altuğ'dan satışı doğrulayan ya da yalanlayan yeni bir açıklama ise henüz yapılmadı.
Cankurt'un aktardığına göre oyuncu, kızı Su dünyaya geldikten sonra mekândan yükselen gürültü yüzünden dairede kalmakta zorlanmış ve yıllar önce başka bir eve taşınmıştı. Altuğ bu sorunu çözmek için hukuki yola da başvurmuş, ancak istediği sonucu alamamıştı. Su'nun bugün Londra'da üniversite okuduğu düşünülürse, Boğaz kıyısındaki bu daire uzun süredir ailenin günlük hayatında yer almıyordu. Satışın tapu kaydı ya da Altuğ'un kendi ağzından bir doğrulaması şimdilik ortaya çıkmadığı için konu, Cankurt'un iddiası olarak gündemde kalmaya devam ediyor.

Trump, Xi and Putin will hold their first trilateral meeting on the sidelines of APEC. With different priorities on trade, Ukraine, Iran and arms control, what does each leader hope to gain?
The leaders of China , the United States and Russia are due to hold their first trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit this week.
Separately, US President Donald Trump will also hold talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping during the November 18-19 gathering in Shenzhen, China.
Several experts interviewed by DW do not expect any breakthroughs on US-China trade, technology or other issues. Maintaining the existing trade truce and preventing bilateral relations from deteriorating further may be the more realistic shared objectives.
Patricia M. Kim, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, believes neither leader is looking to significantly expand the bilateral agenda, as both have an incentive in maintaining the existing trade truce.
Over the next two years, Kim expects to see "neither uncontrolled escalation in tensions between the US and China nor a dramatic improvement in ties, but rather the continuation of the transactional détente we see today."
Zhang Lun, a professor at CY Cergy Paris University, believes Trump is under pressure both at home and abroad.
"Domestically, Trump faces the prospect of becoming a lame-duck president following the Republicans' heavy losses in the midterm elections," Zhang told DW.
"Internationally, damage to relations with allies, the weakening of the US-led international order, indifference toward democratic values and freedoms, and the difficulties encountered in the Iran war have all reduced America's leverage, resources and influence."
Zhang believes strained ties with US allies and the war in Iran have weakened Trump's hand with Beijing, making him more eager to secure diplomatic wins and Xi's cooperation on key policy priorities.
Jia Hui Tee, a senior trade policy analyst at the Hinrich Foundation, expects Trump and Xi to focus on stabilizing their fragile trade relationship.
She says the two leaders could make progress on reciprocal tariff cuts covering goods worth $30 billion (€27.3 billion) on each side. "While the list of products has been announced, the timeline has not been set and an indicative implementation timeline would be an easy win" for both governments.
Washington wants Beijing to accelerate purchases of US agricultural products and increase exports of rare earths and other critical minerals. But Tee believes that "China would likely be cautious with delivering on its commitments especially when Trump is weaker at home after the midterms with Democrats pushing back on his tariffs."
She also points out that neither side would want to cede their bargaining chips easily, including rare earth exports and technology export controls.
With another meeting between the two leaders is expected in December at the G20 summit in Miami, "there is room to push more contentious issues to a later date and further extend the trade truce in the next meeting," Jia told DW.
Russia hopes that talks with the leaders of the US and China will enhance its diplomatic standing and help secure a settlement to the war in Ukraine on terms favorable to Moscow.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center, told DW that Moscow wants to create the impression that Washington is willing to sit down with Russia and negotiate. This, in turn, could undermine confidence in Europe and Ukraine .
"Trump wants trilateral nuclear talks," she said, while Beijing "wants the optics of China hosting the unprecedented historical meeting among the three."
Alicja Bachulska, a policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations, believes Beijing wants to use the meeting to demonstrate its ability to bring major powers together and facilitate international dialogue.
"Russia wants recognition, the US wants arms control, and China wants status without strings attached," she said. "I expect each leader to restate their own positions rather than produce real solutions."
Michael Kimmage, director of the Kennan Institute in the United States, told DW last month that China may be more concerned with the survival of Russian President Vladimir Putin's regime than with actively bringing the war in Ukraine to an end.
Russia remains an important source of energy and a key diplomatic partner for Beijing, Kimmage noted.
An outright Russian victory may not necessarily be Beijing's objective, he said. "More important to China is the political survival of Vladimir Putin." For that reason, Kimmage does not expect China to pressure the Russian president into ending the war if Putin is unwilling to do so.
Zhang Lun believes the current situation is "most in line with Beijing's interests."
The Trump administration's pro-Putin stance has made it harder for Ukraine to resist Russia, Zhang said, while Europe has been forced to bear greater costs and has been weakened.
He argued that the United States has also "lost moral authority" and "the postwar international order and the alliances built around Washington have been further eroded," making China's "position and influence more prominent."
He believes Beijing wants to keep Russia from collapsing, but not support it so openly or extensively that it alienates Europe and other Western countries.
"At the same time, China does not want Ukraine to be defeated, because that would reduce Russia's dependence on Beijing," he told DW.
"For now, China is unlikely to intervene directly. Instead, it will wait for a more favorable moment and then potentially step in as a neutral mediator in order to maximize its gains."
W.A. Figueroa, an assistant professor of history and international relations at the University of Groningen in the Netherlands, told DW that there is little indication of any real cooperation between China and the US on Iran .
The two countries do share some interests, "including opposition to a toll system in the Strait of Hormuz and opposition to nuclear proliferation," Figueroa noted, but "China has consistently called for negotiations and denounced both sanctions and military force as a way to achieve these or any other objectives."
Figueroa says China does not want further escalation or prolonged instability in the Middle East. However, Beijing has been able to manage the current situation without too much difficulty, leaving it with little pressure to change its position.
"China continues to provide Iran with crucial financial support through its purchases of Iranian oil," Figueroa noted, adding that Beijing's diplomatic support has so far brought no substantial change, largely because China has little leverage over either Iran or the US in the region.

Haitians take to the streets to praise El Salvador’s Nayib Bukele and his soldiers for fighting gangs in the country.
Thousands of Haitians have taken to the streets of Port-au-Prince to show support for soldiers from El Salvador, deployed by President Nayib Bukele to confront armed gangs that control large sections of the capital.
Protesters on Tuesday carried signs reading “Thank you, Bukele” and “Long live Bukele”.
Bukele has sent more than 2,000 troops to Haiti since late October, after four soldiers from El Salvador went missing during an operation by the United Nations-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF).
The latest Salvadoran deployment, although separate from the GSF, has been welcomed by Haitian authorities, who have long sought additional reinforcements to combat the gangs.
Bukele’s hardline crackdown on gangs in El Salvador has broad public support but has drawn accusations of human rights violations.
On November 10, he claimed to have destroyed the “headquarters” of one of Haiti’s main gangs, releasing video footage of a helicopter attack.
Since then, Salvadoran forces, backed by Haiti’s national police, have taken control of a football stadium in the capital.
On Tuesday, the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights urged all security forces in Haiti to prioritise the protection of civilians and to use lethal force only as a measure of last resort.
In the first 10 months of this year, the UN recorded 4,595 killings and 2,050 injuries linked to armed violence in Haiti.
Haiti, the poorest country in the Americas, has faced a deepening political and security crisis, with gangs tightening their grip on the country through a campaign of violence marked by murder, kidnapping and rape.

Nvidia, 2027 mali yılının üçüncü çeyreği olarak kabul ettiği 25 Ekim'de sona eren üç aylık dönemin finansal sonuçlarına ilişkin telekonferans düzenledi.
Şirketin Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Harvey Jones, buradaki konuşmasında, Nvidia'nın son derece güçlü bir şirket olduğunu, finansal performansının da bunu açıkça ortaya koyduğunu söyledi.
Yönetim Kurulunun 12 Kasım'da şirketin davranış kuralları, standartları ve kurum kültürüyle bağdaşmayan kişisel davranışlarının ortaya çıkmasının ardından Jensen Huang'ın başkanlık, CEO'luk ve yönetim kurulu üyeliği görevlerinden kendi isteğiyle istifa ettiğini duyurduğunu anımsatan Jones, Huang'ın istifasının oy birliğiyle kabul edildiğini ve kendisini yeniden CEO olarak görevlendirme niyetinde olmadıklarını aktardı.
Jones, Huang'ın istifasına ilişkin koşullar ve devam eden soruşturma hakkında herhangi bir açıklama yapmayacaklarını ve bu konudaki soruları yanıtlamayacaklarını belirtti.
Yeni CEO'nun belirlenmesi sürecinde şirket içinden ve dışından adayların değerlendirileceğini aktaran Jones, gelişmiş çip teknolojileri ve ulusal güvenlik dinamiklerinin sektörde büyük değişimlere yol açtığını, yeni CEO'nun bu koşulları çok dikkatli şekilde yönetmesi gerekeceğini ifade etti.
Jones, kalıcı CEO'nun mümkün olan en kısa sürede göreve getirilmesini istediklerini ancak doğru adayı bulmadan atama sürecini aceleye getirmeyeceklerini kaydetti.
Nvidia'nın geçici CEO'su ve Finans Direktörü (CFO) Colette Kress de iş açısından bakıldığında şirkette her şeyin alışılageldiği şekilde sürdüğünü belirtti.
Şirketin müşterileri, tedarikçileri ve iş ortaklarıyla iletişim halinde olduklarını anlatan Kress, "Hepsi de bizi yüzde 100 destekliyor. Müşterilerimiz, iş görünümüne desteklerini ve bu süreçte bize yardımcı olma isteklerini dile getiriyor. Ayrıca, arz ve talep arasındaki boşlukları daraltmak için tedarikçilerimizle de yakın bir işbirliği içinde çalışıyorlar." diye konuştu.
Son dönemde ​​​​​​​Huang'ın aralarında Çin adına casusluk yaptığı öne sürülen bir kadınla yaşadığı dahil evlilik dışı ilişkileriyle ilgili haberlerle gündeme gelen Nvidia'nın finansal sonuçlarına ilişkin düzenlediği telekonferans, piyasalar ve yatırımcılar tarafından yakından takip edildi.
Nvidia Yönetim Kurulu, 8 Kasım'da Jensen Huang'ın yabancı istihbarat faaliyetinin hedefi olduğuna ilişkin haberlerin ardından bağımsız soruşturma başlatıldığını duyurmuştu.
Öte yandan The New York Times gazetesinde yayımlanan bir haberde, Huang'ın şirkette kendisine bağlı bir yöneticiyle de evlilik dışı ilişki yaşadığı iddia edilmişti.
Nvidia 12 Kasım'da ise Huang'ın başkanlık, üst yöneticilik ve yönetim kurulu üyeliği görevlerinden derhal geçerli olmak üzere ayrıldığını, şirketin başkan yardımcısı ve finans direktörü Colette Kress'in geçici CEO olarak atandığını bildirmişti.
Nvidia'dan ayrılmasının ardından dün ilk kez açıklama yapan Huang, Yönetim Kurulunun geri dönmesinin hissedarların, çalışanların, şirketin ve ABD'nin çıkarları için en iyisi olacağına karar vermesi halinde CEO olarak görevine dönmeye hazır olduğunu ifade etmişti.

Chinese President Xi Jinping called on Wednesday for stronger global cooperation on artificial intelligence and free trade, as he opened the APEC summit in Shenzhen ahead of an expected meeting with US President Donald Trump. Trade tensions and new US chip export restrictions are set to feature prominently.
Chinese President Xi Jinping called on Wednesday for greater international cooperation on AI and free trade, as pressure grows on world powers to do more to address the risks of the groundbreaking technology.
Xi made the remarks as he formally opened an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen, where he is expected to meet US President Donald Trump on Thursday.
"We should actively build partnerships for scientific and technological innovation, deepen cooperation in the digital economy and artificial intelligence and promote a green and low-carbon transition," the Chinese leader said.
"By continuously transforming our innovation strengths into growth momentum, we can provide a robust impetus for economic growth in the Asia-Pacific and foster shared prosperity across the region."
Read more China to host first-ever trilateral meeting between Trump, Xi and Putin next week
Xi also called for the elimination of trade and investment barriers, saying that it was crucial to "promote inclusive and balanced development".
He said China sought to "provide a more stable, predictable and beneficial environment for global enterprises" and would continue to expand access in its manufacturing and services sectors.
"Starting by lowering tariffs , expanding access and exploring regulations and management standards, China will conduct deep-seated reform," Xi said.
Trade tensions have been looming over the leaders of the world's two largest economies as the summit has approached.

Heavy metal tarihinin en büyük ve en etkili gruplarından Judas Priest , 17 Temmuz 2027'de İstanbul’da müzikseverlerle buluşmaya hazırlanıyor. Metal müziğin gelişimine yön veren, kendine özgü sound’u ve sahne enerjisiyle kuşaklar boyunca müzisyenlere ve dinleyicilere ilham veren efsane grup Judas Priest, İstanbul'a geliyor. Grup Epifoni ve URU ortak organizasyonuyla 17 Temmuz 2027'de KüçükÇiftlik Park sahnesinde olacak.
1969 yılında İngiltere’nin Birmingham kentinde kurulan Judas Priest, yarım asrı aşan kariyeri boyunca heavy metalin yalnızca müzikal sınırlarını değil, sahne kültürünü ve görsel kimliğini de şekillendiren grupların başında geliyor. Rob Halford’un benzersiz vokali, güçlü gitar riffleri ve grubun karakteristik çift gitar sound’u, Judas Priest’i metal tarihinin en belirleyici isimlerinden biri haline getirdi.
“Breaking the Law”, “Living After Midnight”, “You’ve Got Another Thing Comin’”, “Painkiller” ve “Electric Eye” gibi kuşaklar boyunca hafızalara kazınan şarkılara imza atan grup; British Steel, Screaming for Vengeance, Defenders of the Faith ve Painkiller gibi klasik albümleriyle heavy metalin kilometre taşlarını oluşturdu. 50 milyonu aşan albüm satışı ve 2022 yılında Rock & Roll Hall of Fame’e kabul edilmesi de grubun müzik tarihindeki ayrıcalıklı yerini tescilledi.
Siyah deri ve metal aksesuarlarla özdeşleşen ikonik tarzı, sahnedeki güçlü duruşu ve zamana meydan okuyan şarkılarıyla Judas Priest, bugün de heavy metalin en önemli temsilcilerinden biri olmayı sürdürüyor.

Mavi Alan Perge Salonu'ndaki "Toroslar'dan Küresel İklim Eylemine: İklim Dirençliliği İçin Yörük Bilgeliği" başlıklı panelde, geleneksel Yörük yaşam biçiminin doğal kaynakların korunması, sürdürülebilirlik ve iklim değişikliğine uyum açısından taşıdığı önem değerlendirildi.
Yörükler Kültür Dayanışma ve Yardımlaşma Derneği Başkanı Abdullah Duman, panelde yaptığı konuşmada, Yörük kültürünün, sürdürülebilirliği bir kavram olarak değil, bir yaşam biçimi olarak asırlardır uyguladığını söyledi.
Geleneksel Yörük yaşamında atık kavramına rastlamanın zor olduğunu belirten Duman, "Çünkü yeniden kullanım, tasarruf, onarım ve israftan kaçınmak, günlük hayatın doğal bir parçasıdır." dedi.
Yörüklerin kullandığı eşyaların ahşap, deri, yün, kıl ve dokuma gibi doğal malzemelerden oluştuğunu aktaran Duman, doğayla uyumlu yaşam biçiminin gelecek kuşaklara aktarılmasının önemini vurguladı.
Yörük kültürünün yalnızca folklorik bir miras olarak görülmemesi gerektiğini belirten Duman, "Yörük kültürü, tabiatın yaşayan ekolojik arşividir. Bu hafızayı korumak, doğanın bilgisini geleceğe taşımaktır. Bizim amacımız, geçmişin yaşam biçimini birebir tekrarlamak değil, o yaşam biçiminin arkasındaki ekolojik zekayı, felsefeyi ve doğa bilincini insanlığa kazandırmaktır." diye konuştu.
Duman, Yörüklerin geçmişten gelen bilgi birikiminin çevresel sorunlara çözüm sunabileceğine dikkati çekti.
Antalya Gazeteciler Cemiyeti Başkanı İdris Taş da Yörük yaşamının doğayla kurduğu ilişkiye değindi.
Toroslar'da şekillenen Yörük kültürünün doğadaki tüm canlılara saygıyı esas aldığını kaydeden Taş, geleneksel yaşam biçiminde insanların doğanın sahibi değil, bir parçası olarak görüldüğünü ifade etti.
Taş, Yörüklerin yaşam kültüründe hayvanlara, bitkilere ve doğal yaşama zarar vermeden var olma anlayışının öne çıktığını dile getirdi.
Panelde, Akdeniz Üniversitesi Ziraat Fakültesinden Prof. Dr. Orhan Özçatalbaş, İstanbul Teknik Üniversitesinden Prof. Dr. İsmail Koyuncu, Antalya İş İnsanları Derneği Başkanı ve Yörük İl Beyi Bilal Köleoğlu da konuşma yaptı.

Lezzetiyle öne çıkan yerli muz, başta Ermenistan Başbakanı Nikol Paşinyan olmak üzere devlet başkanlarının, bakanların, bürokratların ve katılımcıların beğenisini topladı.
Manavgat'ta muz üreticiliği yapan Öncel Grup Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Şevki Öncel, AA muhabirine, yaklaşık 10 yıldır muz yetiştirdiklerini ve yaklaşık 300 dekarlık örtü altı alanında 2 bin ton üretim yaptıklarını söyledi.
Yerli muzun ithal muzdan daha lezzetli olduğunu dile getiren Öncel, bunu da daha organik koşullarda üretim yapmalarına bağladı.
İthal muzun 45 günlük yoldan geldiği için nakliye süresince öz suyunu harcadığını anlatan Öncel, yerli muza kıyasla hem lezzet hem de yararlı özellikler bakımından yoksun kaldığını​​​​​​​ ifade etti.
Yerli muzda ise meyve olgunlaştığında hasat yapıldığını belirten Öncel, "Bizim ürünümüz hem doğal hem lezzetli hem de faydaları saymakla bitmez çünkü doğal gübreyle yetiştiriyoruz. Topraklarımızda mineral elementler daha zengin. Ürünün tüketilmesinden bir hafta önce hasat ediyoruz." diye konuştu.
Öncel, örtü altında üretim ile iklimi de kontrol edebildiklerini, 12 ay boyunca ürün yetiştirebildiklerini kaydetti.
Ürünlerini sadece iç piyasaya sunduklarını söyleyen Öncel, tüketicilere yerli muzu tercih etmelerini önerdi.
Antalya'da düzenlenen COP31'de liderlere de yerli muzun ikram edildiğini belirten Öncel, "Devlet görevlilerine, diğer protokol üyelerine bizden çok hediyelik tropik meyve ve muz götürüldü. Otellerimiz de yerli muzu tercih ediyor. Katılımcılar konakladıkları otellerde de Antalya'nın ürünlerini tüketti." diye konuştu.
Muz üreticiliği yapan Ziraat Yüksek Mühendisi Osman Çavuşoğlu da muzun tropikal iklim bitkisi olduğunu ve buna göre üretim yaptıklarını söyledi.
Muz üretiminde gece-gündüz, yaz-kış sıcaklıkları farkının çok olmaması gerektiğini vurgulayan Çavuşoğlu, "16-33 santigrat derece arasında sıcaklık ve yüzde 60-80 arasında nem isteyen bir bitkidir. Bunun yanında organik maddece zengin geçirgen bir toprak yapısını seven bir üründür. Antalya buna elverişli bir iklime sahip." dedi.
Çavuşoğlu, yerli muz ile ithal muzu yiyenlerin arasındaki farkı çok rahat fark edebildiğini kaydetti.

İspanyol futbolunun efsane ismi Juan Mata , yaklaşık 20 yıllık profesyonel kariyerini 18 Kasım’da yayımladığı veda mesajıyla noktaladı.
Son iki sezonunu Avustralya’da geçiren İspanyol orta saha oyuncusu, sosyal medya paylaşımında “ Bazen sevmek, bırakabilmektir. Teşekkürler futbol ” ifadelerini kullandı.
Real Madrid altyapısında yetişen Mata, adını Valencia’da duyurdu ve 2008’de İspanya Kral Kupası’nı kazandı. İspanya’nın 2010 Dünya Kupası’nı kazanan kadrosunda yer alan futbolcu, iki yıl sonra Avrupa Şampiyonası finalinde İtalya’ya karşı gol attı.
2011’de Chelsea’ye transfer olan Mata, Londra ekibiyle 2012’de Şampiyonlar Ligi, 2013’te UEFA Avrupa Ligi kupasını kaldırdı. Ocak 2014’te Manchester United’a geçen İspanyol futbolcu, 2017’de Avrupa Ligi’ni bu kez Manchester ekibiyle kazandı.
Mata, Manchester United’dan ayrıldıktan sonra 2022 yazında Galatasaray ’a katıldı. Sarı-kırmızılı formayla 18 maçta üç gol atan İspanyol futbolcu, 2022-23 sezonunda Süper Lig şampiyonluğu yaşadı.
Ardından Japonya’da Vissel Kobe, Avustralya’da ise Western Sydney Wanderers ve Melbourne Victory’de forma giydi.
Melbourne Victory’de geçirdiği son sezonda Avustralya liginin en iyi oyuncusuna verilen Johnny Warren Madalyası’nı kazanan Mata, eylülde kulüpteki oyunculuk dönemini sonlandırmıştı.
Melbourne Victory’nin hissedarları arasında yer alan Mata, kulübün futbol komitesinin başkanlığını üstlenecek.

Sosyal medya hesabından kararını duyuran İspanyol futbolcu Juan Mata, futbola teşekkür etti. Mata ayrıca kramponlarını astığı görüntülerin olduğu bir video paylaştı.
Futbolculuk kariyerine Real Oviedo altyapısında başlayan ve daha sonra Real Madrid altyapısına geçen 38 yaşındaki futbolcu; Valencia, Chelsea, Manchester United, Galatasaray, Vissel Kobe, Western Sydney Wanderers ve Melbourne Victory'de forma giydi.
Kulüp kariyerinde 699 resmi çıkan Juan Mata, 148 gol, 166 asistlik performans sergiledi. İspanya Milli Takımı ile de 41 karşılaşmada görev yapan ve 10 gol sevinci yaşayan Mata, 2010 yılında Dünya Kupası'nı, 2012 yılında da Avrupa Şampiyonası'nı kazandı. Deneyimli futbolcu, Chelsea ile 2012'de UEFA Şampiyonlar Ligi şampiyonu oldu.
İspanyol futbolcu ayrıca UEFA Şampiyonlar Ligi'nde 1, UEFA Avrupa Ligi'nde 2, FA Cup'ta 2, EFL Cup'ta 1, Community Shield'da 1, Copa del Rey'de 1, Trendyol Süper Lig'de 1 ve Japonya 1. Futbol Ligi'nde de 1 şampiyonluk yaşadı.

Antalya'da düzenlenen COP31'in "Okyanus, Denizler, Doğa ve Arazi Kullanımı" teması kapsamında, mercan resiflerinin korunmasına yönelik yeni finansman kararları duyuruldu. BM Çevre Programı (UNEP) tarafından yayımlanan açıklamaya göre, Küresel Mercan Resifleri Fonu (GFCR), 22 gelişmekte olan ülkede mercan resiflerinin korunması ve kıyı toplumlarının iklim değişikliğine karşı dayanıklılığının artırılması amacıyla 30 milyon doların üzerinde yeni yatırım ve bağış taahhüdü açıkladı.
UNEP'in değerlendirilmesine göre, sıcak ve sığ su mercan resifi ekosistemlerinin yüzde 96'sının kritik tehlike altında bulunduğu belirtildi. Deniz suyu sıcaklıklarının yükselmesi, denizlerdeki sıcak hava dalgaları, kirlilik, aşırı avlanma ve kıyı yapılaşmasının mercan resiflerini tehdit ettiği vurgulandı. Bilimsel projeksiyonlara göre, küresel sıcaklık artışının 2 dereceye ulaşması durumunda günümüzdeki mercan resiflerinin yüzde 1'inden daha azının sağlıklı kalabileceği uyarısı yapıldı.
Yeni finansman paketi kapsamında mercan resiflerinin korunması, deniz koruma alanlarının güçlendirilmesi, sürdürülebilir balıkçılığın desteklenmesi ve kıyı toplumları için alternatif geçim kaynaklarının oluşturulması hedefleniyor. Açıklanan kaynağın 10 milyon doların üzerindeki bölümünü GFCR Yönetim Kurulu tarafından onaylanan yeni yatırımlar, 20 milyon doların üzerindeki bölümünü ise ülkelerin yeni ve yenilenen finansman taahhütleri oluşturuyor.
Mercan resiflerinin yalnızca deniz canlıları açısından değil, milyonlarca insanın geçim kaynakları bakımından da büyük önem taşıdığı belirtildi. Resiflerin balıklar ve diğer deniz canlıları için yaşam alanı oluşturduğu, balıkçılığı ve turizmi desteklediği, kıyıları fırtınaların etkilerine karşı koruduğu kaydedildi. Resiflerin yok olmasının biyolojik çeşitlilik kaybının yanı sıra gıda güvenliği ve kıyı ekonomileri açısından da ciddi sonuçlar doğurabileceğine dikkat çekildi.
Yeni yatırımlar kapsamında Meksika, Belize, Guatemala ve Honduras'ı kapsayan Mezoamerika Resifi bölgesindeki 18 öncelikli alanda koruma ve finansman çalışmalarının genişletilmesi planlanıyor. Atık su arıtımı, deniz ekosistemlerinin korunması, küçük ölçekli balıkçılara kredi ve sigorta desteği gibi uygulamalarla 12 milyon dolarlık ek finansmanın harekete geçirilmesi hedefleniyor.
Endonezya'da deniz yosunu yetiştiriciliği, balıkçılık ve atık yönetimi alanlarında çevre dostu işletmeler desteklenecek. Filipinler'de yaklaşık 1 milyon hektarlık deniz koruma alanının yönetiminin güçlendirilmesi ve 1,1 milyondan fazla kişinin yaşadığı kıyı topluluklarına ekonomik katkı sağlanması amaçlanıyor. Tanzanya'ya bağlı Zanzibar'da ise deniz koruma çalışmalarıyla 21 bin kıyı sakininin iklim değişikliğine uyum kapasitesinin artırılması öngörülüyor.
Pasifik ülkelerinde de mercan resiflerinin korunmasına yönelik yeni finansman mekanizmaları hayata geçiriliyor. Fiji'de çevre dostu işletmelere kredi sağlayacak bir finansman mekanizması faaliyete geçerken, Solomon Adaları'nda Mavi Ekonomi Finansman Mekanizması başlatıldı. Papua Yeni Gine'de ise 50'den fazla çevre dostu işletmeye uygun koşullu kredi sağlandığı açıklandı.
UNEP İcra Direktörü Inger Andersen, mercan resiflerini iklim değişikliği, kirlilik ve diğer tehditlerden korumak için zamanla yarıştıklarını belirtti. Mercan resiflerinin korunması ve restorasyonuna kararlı yatırımlar yapıldığında yeniden toparlanabildiğini vurgulayan Andersen, bu yatırımların biyolojik çeşitliliğin korunmasının yanı sıra balıkçılık, geçim kaynakları ve kıyı toplumlarının dayanıklılığına katkı sağladığını ifade etti.
BM Kalkınma Programı (UNDP) Başkanı Alexander De Croo da mercan resiflerinin milyonlarca insan için gıda ve geçim kaynağı olduğunu, kıyıları fırtınalardan koruduğunu belirterek, kaybedilmelerinin yalnızca ekolojik değil, ekonomik bir felakete de yol açabileceği uyarısında bulundu.
Küresel Mercan Resifleri Fonu, 2030 yılına kadar en az 400 çevre dostu işletme ve finansman çözümünü desteklemeyi, 3 milyon hektarlık iklim değişikliğine dayanıklı mercan resifinin yönetimini iyileştirmeyi ve 20 milyon insanın iklim değişikliğine karşı dayanıklılığını artırmayı hedefliyor. Bu alanın dünyadaki mercan resiflerinin yüzde 10'undan fazlasına karşılık geldiği belirtildi.

texts.https://tr.euronews.com/2026/11/18/rober:
Robert Pattinson'ın resmi olarak yedinci James Bond olarak seçilmesiyle söylentiler dönemi artık kapandı. Oyuncu bu rolü "hayatımın en büyük onuru" ve "gerçekleşen bir rüya" diye tanımladı.
Tepkiler yer yer karışık olsa da genel olarak olumlu , ancak şimdi Amazon'un patronu Jeff Bezos'un oyuncu seçiminde rol oynadığı ortaya çıktı.
Kaliforniya'da bir etkinlikte konuşan Bezos, izleyicilere oyuncu seçimi sürecine "yoğun biçimde dahil olduğunu" söyledi. İngiliz oyuncunun zaten ünlü olması nedeniyle bazı kaygılar bulunmasına rağmen Pattinson'ın neden seçildiğini anlattı, böylece Bond'un yükselen bir oyuncu tarafından canlandırılması gerektiğine dair yazılı olmayan kural fiilen bozulmuş oldu.
Bezos, "Başta, onun zaten çok ünlü olması nedeniyle kendisine karşı biraz önyargılı olduğumuzu söyleyebilirim," diye konuştu. "Belki biraz daha az tanınan birini seçmemiz gerektiğini düşünmüştük."
Sözlerini şöyle sürdürdü: "Ama deneme çekiminde o kadar barizdi ki. O, James Bond."
Bezos, bir sonraki 007 için seçilen son beş oyuncunun "olağanüstü yetenekli" olduğunu, ancak Rob'da "özel bir şey" bulunduğunu da söyledi.
Pattinson'ın Bond olarak ilk filmi, ünlü serinin arkasındaki Hollywood stüdyosu MGM'nin Amazon tarafından satın alınmasından bu yana gösterime girecek ilk Bond filmi olacak.
Onun seçilmesi, eğlence sektörünün içinde ve dışında birçok isimden yüksek övgü aldı.
Kraliyet ailesi, oyuncu seçimini resmi Instagram hesaplarından "Majestelerinin Gizli Servisi'ne hoş geldiniz Bay Bond" notuyla paylaştı. Birleşik Krallık Başbakanı Andy Burnham'ın bir sözcüsü ise başbakanın "Robert Pattinson adına açıkça çok mutlu olduğunu" ve rolün "muhteşem bir fırsat" olduğunu söyledi.
Okyanusun öte yakasında, Donald Trump'ın sağlık bakanı Robert F. Kennedy Jr da işe katılmanın iyi bir fikir olduğuna karar vererek, sürpriz olmayan bir şekilde , kendisini 007 olarak gösteren yapay zeka üretimi bir görsel paylaştı. Görselde silahın yerini dev bir havuç alıyordu ve gönderinin açıklamasında "Yemek. Gerçek yemek." yazıyordu.
İnternet kullanıcıları paylaşımı hızla alaya aldı ve Trump'ın kabinesinin etraftaki en ciddiyetsiz kişiler olduğu gerçeğine vurgu yaptı. Bir yorumda "Bu bok için kim oy verdi?" ifadesi yer alırken, başka bir kullanıcı "Amerika'nın ihtiyacı gıda güvenliği, Sebze Bond rolü için seçmelere katılan bir kabine bakanı değil" diye yazdı.
Çok daha ciddi bir not olarak, Bond 26'nın yönetmeni Denis Villeneuve, GQ'ya verdiği bir röportajda kendi 007'sini ararken baktığı en önemli nitelikleri anlattı.
Prisoners , Sicario , Blade Runner 2049 ve Dune filmlerinin arkasındaki, Oscar'a aday gösterilmiş Kanadalı yönetmen şöyle konuştu: "İlk özellik, bu adamın bir katil olduğuna inanabilmem. Çünkü Bond, bir casustan çok bir suikastçı. Gözlerin derininde o türden bir öfke görmem gerekiyor. Herkeste böyle bir şey yok."
Sözlerini şöyle sürdürdü: "Özür dilemeyen bir gösterişe sahip birine ihtiyacım var, odaya girdiği anda her şeyin etrafında toplanmaya başladığı, o türden güçlü bir karizması olan ve aynı zamanda çok fazla çekiciliği bulunan, insanların kendisine kapıldığı biri... Karanlık mizahı olan, derin bokun içinde olmaktan zevk alan, elini çamura sokmaktan korkmayan biri. Güçlü, kaslı, adeta bir güç olan birine ihtiyacım var. Ve elbette, gözlerinde derin bir zekâ taşıyan, bizden her zaman bir adım önde olan biri."
Villeneuve daha önce henüz gösterime girmemiş Dune: Part Three 'de Pattinson ile birlikte çalışmıştı.
Öte yandan, çok sayıda ünlü isim de Pattinson'ın seçimini övdü.
Daniel Craig'in veda macerası No Time to Die 'da Safin adlı kötü karakteri canlandıran Rami Malek, Pattinson'ın 007 olarak "olağanüstü" olacağını söyledi.
Mumbai'deki Earthshot Ödülleri'nde konuşan Malek, "Rob'u epey uzun zamandır tanıyorum ve daha fazla gurur duyamazdım. İnsanların, bence belki de herkesin, o adamın ne kadar yetenekli olduğunu fark etmesi gerçeği" dedi.
Skyfall , Spectre ve No Time To Die 'da M'i canlandıran (ve Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire 'da Pattinson'ı öldüren) Ralph Fiennes, SiriusXM Front Row'da Andy Cohen'le yaptığı röportajda, "Üzgünüm. Ben hâlâ Daniel Craig'e âşığım," dedi, ardından Pattinson'ın görevin üstesinden geleceğine inandığını ekledi. "Hayır, o harika bir oyuncu," diye konuştu. "Eminim harika olacaktır."
Pattinson'ın Tenet 'teki rol arkadaşı Elizabeth Debicki, oyuncu için "çok heyecanlı" olduğunu ve ona göre Pattinson'ın "mükemmel Bond" olacağını söyledi.
Variety (kaynak İngilizce) 'nin aktardığına göre Debicki, "Kendisi başlı başına bir bilmece. Çok yakışıklı, komik ve zeki... Bence o mükemmel. Çok heyecanlıyım," dedi ve "Bir oyuncu olarak çok gelişti. Gerçekten ilginç seçimler yaptı. Gerçekten zeki" diye ekledi.
Hollywood yıldızı Brad Pitt de Pattinson'ın göreve getirilmesini kamuoyu önünde destekleyerek, kırmızı halıda muhabirlere şunları söyledi: "Bu fikri seviyorum. Yaptıklarını seviyorum. Seçimlerini seviyorum ve bence o gerçekten sahici. Harika. İyi seçim." Pitt ayrıca, Pattinson'ın filmlerinden birinde gelecekteki bir Bond kötü adamını oynaması fikrine karşı olmayacağını da esprili bir dille ekledi.
Önceki Bond'lara gelince, hayatta olan en yaşlı 007 oyuncusu George Lazenby, Robert Pattinson'ı aralarına hoş geldi.
1969 yapımı On Her Majesty’s Secret Service 'de bir kez Bond'u canlandıran 87 yaşındaki Lazenby, Pattinson'ı kulübe hoş geldin diyerek karşılayan bir video mesajını Instagram'da paylaştı.
"Robert, dünyadaki en ayrıcalıklı kulübe hoş geldin," diyen Lazenby, ardından şu tavsiyeyi verdi: "Ama kendini eğlendirmeyi unutma. Bakalım senin de 'diğer adama hiç böyle bir şey olmamıştı' anın olacak mı." Lazenby sözlerini "En iyisi senin için dostum, George" diyerek noktaladı.
Pattinson, sinemada James Bond'u canlandırmış yalnızca altı oyuncunun izinden gidiyor; Sean Connery, Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan ve Craig.
Henüz adı açıklanmayan Bond 26'nın vizyona girmesi konusunda ise izleyicilerin biraz daha beklemesi gerekecek.
Çekimlerin gelecek yıl başlaması bekleniyor. Ancak Pattinson'ın, yönetmen Matt Reeves'in kişisel bir sorunla karşılaşması üzerine geçici olarak durdurulmuştu olan The Batman Part II 'nin çekimlerini tamamlaması gerekiyor. Filmin son birkaç haftasının çekilmesine yardımcı olmak için Steven Soderbergh devreye girdi.
Bu da, bir sonraki Bond macerasını en erken 2028'in ikinci yarısında görebileceğimiz anlamına geliyor ve No Time To Die 'dan bu yana yedi yıl geçmiş olacak. Bu süre, 1989 yapımı Licence To Kill ile 1995 yapımı GoldenEye arasındaki dönemden bu yana Bond filmleri arasındaki en uzun boşluğu oluşturacak.
