A wonder strike from Justin Devenny earned Northern Ireland top spot in Nations League Group B2 and promotion to the top tier of the competition. The Stoke player fired home on the volley from the edge of the area to earn a 1-1 draw away to Hungary , who would have leapfrogged Michael O’Neill’s side in the group with victory.
Northern Ireland had fallen 1-0 behind after a 35th-minute goal from the striker Barnabas Varga, who slotted home when one-on-one with the goalkeeper Pierce Charles after a defensive mix-up. The goal ended Northern Ireland’s proud record of not having conceded in this campaign and also sent Hungary to the top of the group in the live standings.
But moments after Isaac Price had hit the post for O’Neill’s young outfit, Devenny smashed the ball into the top left-hand corner in the 65th minute to restore Northern Ireland’s one-point advantage as group leaders. As time ticked down, Hungary pushed forward in increasing desperation – with Rajmund Toth firing over late on – but Northern Ireland dug in with the defensive resilience which has been the cornerstone of their campaign.
“It’s a great feeling for us,” said O’Neill, who had to watch the game from the stands as he served a touchline ban. “We set out when we came into this level of the competition to first of all try and stay and we knew to be in the top two positions would help us.
“We knew that would help us potentially with the draw for Euro 2028 [qualification] but to come away unbeaten, to finish top, and to give the performance we’ve given against some very good teams, it’s very encouraging.”
In Wales’s group, Norway snatched a quarter-final berth thanks to Erling Haaland’s 96th-minute penalty against Denmark . It was Haaland’s second and completed a remarkable comeback from 2-0 down as the Danes were pipped for second place in Group A4.
Denmark, who began the day in second place in the standings and needed to avoid defeat to reach the knockout phase, led 2-0 inside 14 minutes through Rasmus Højlund and Pierre-Emile Højbjerg.
But Haaland pulled one back before half-time and, after Martin Ødegaard’s 83rd-minute equaliser had set up a grandstand finish, the Manchester City striker scored from the spot in the sixth minute of added time after the video assistant referee had ruled Joachim Andersen had handled in the area.
The two nations finished level on nine points and although Denmark had a better goal difference, Norway progressed on their head-to-head record after also winning the reverse fixture 3-2.
“It’s one of the crazier football years,” Haaland told TV2. “It’s fun to be a part of finishing it off in style. Ståle [Solbakken, Norway’s coach] said ⁠it before the match: ‘Let’s just get a good finish now to a completely indescribable football year.’ It’s fun to be Norwegian.”
Norway’s latest success came ​on the back of their memorable World Cup run, when Haaland ‌and Ødegaard led the country to the ‌quarter-finals in their first appearance at the tournament for 28 years. “It’s completely fantastic and fun,” Haaland said. “I should have had a hat-trick today, ‌but I’m happy with two goals, so that’s totally fine.”
The Republic of Ireland beat 10-man Kosovo 3-0 at the Aviva Stadium to go ahead of the visitors in the standings for Group B3 to secure second place and a spot in the promotion playoffs. The win also propelled the Euro 2028 co-hosts into a coveted pot-two seeding for next month’s qualifying draw for that competition.
Kreshnik Hajrizi’s first-half handball on the line earned the Kosovo defender a red card and allowed Troy Parrott to bury the resulting penalty. The Republic were awarded a second spot-kick early in the second period after a foul by the goalkeeper Arijanet Muric, with Parrott again scoring. Jack Moylan’s header from a Liam Kitching cross made it 3-0.
What had been a largely uneventful encounter took a dramatic twist in the 26th minute, the red card incident sparked by Moylan’s cross, glanced on by Liam Scales to Parrott. His effort – clearly goalbound – was cleared off the line by Hajrizi, who extended his arm like a goalkeeper, and was immediately sent off.

The battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster and the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer. It could be a tipping point in the industry
T he awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but.
Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history. It is expected to fetch between $1.5bn and $2bn, with some predicting the outcome could be a landmark moment for the sports and entertainment industry.
There also appears to be a clear frontrunner. “I would put money on Netflix to win – they will pay whatever it takes,” one experienced media rights buyer told the Guardian.
Multiple sources have confirmed that Netflix will submit a bid ahead of Thursday’s deadline for first-round offers, along with fellow streamers Apple TV, Disney, Amazon, YouTube and Dazn, as well as the traditional broadcasting heavyweights, Fox, ESPN, NBC Universal and Paramount Skydance, although the latter may find itself constrained by the ongoing budget cuts being made after its $110bn acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery. Netflix has already bought exclusive rights in the US for the 2027 and 2031 Women’s World Cup.
“There’s a huge range of buyers and therefore a broad range of possible outcomes,” one broadcasting veteran says. “All the media companies and streamers will bid. Fox will find it very challenging to retain the rights.”
In a significant change, Fifa is selling the English and Spanish rights together for the first time in an attempt that indicates it is seeking a single exclusive rights holder, which would suit the streaming companies. With Fox having paid $485m for exclusive English-language rights to the 2026 World Cup, and NBC Universal’s Telemundo paying $600m for the Spanish-language rights, the only certainty is that the 2030 price will be far higher, despite less attractive kick-off times for a US audience with the tournament in Morocco, Spain and Portugal.
The impact of the time difference is hard to price, but may not prove to be that significant given the seemingly insatiable demand. NBC paid about $1.5bn for exclusive rights for the 2024 Paris Olympics and were rewarded with average daily viewing figures of more than 30 million, albeit with far more variation in programming than a World Cup.
Fifa awarded non-competitive extensions to Fox and Telemundo in 2015 as compensation for moving the 2022 Qatar World Cup to winter, a perspective that was strengthened on the back of this year’s record-breaking tournament. Fox’s live coverage of Spain’s extra-time victory over Argentina in the final was the most-watched soccer telecast in US history, with a peak audience of 51.685 million; five World Cup games brought in average audiences of more than 20 million; and the average viewing figure across all 104 matches was 7.7 million, twice the figure in Qatar four years earlier.
Telemundo’s coverage, available through NBC’s streaming platform Peacock, averaged a total audience of six million viewers per game, with both Spain v Argentina and Mexico v England attracting peak audiences of more than 23 million, the highest-ever for a Spanish-language broadcast in the US.
The bumper audiences were extremely lucrative for the broadcasters, with figures from advertising sales analysts Guideline showing that Fox and Telemundo generated a combined $1.19bn in advertising revenue alone during the tournament, almost three times the figure from Qatar four years earlier and more than their original rights investment.
Fox alone brought in $835m from World Cup advertising, with 30-second slots costing between $200,000 and $750,000 according to the Hollywood Reporter, and the six-minute hydration breaks generating between $2m and $9m per game.
Having left a considerable amount of money on the table due to the circumstances of the 2026 process, Fifa is determined to cash in this time around. Holding the auction only four months after the US hosted the World Cup appears a clear attempt to capitalise on the success of the previous tournament, which contributed the vast majority of Fifa’s $4bn media revenues over the four-year cycle to 2026.
The addition of hydration breaks will give the likes of Fox more revenue to play with, although Fifa will expect the option for extra adverts to drive up the price and take its own cut this time around having missed out in the summer. The two three-minute breaks in each half were only finalised last year and did not feature in the 2026 tender documents.
“Sports advertising is much more valuable than entertainment programming as it has a broader reach,” saysFrançois Godard, an independent media analyst. “And one-off events such as World Cups do not generally do particularly well for subscription services, who want year-round content.
“Fox in particular needs the World Cup and is heavily associated with it. They are the smallest of the legacy broadcasters and are reliant on sport, as well as news. Having said that, the market for sport amongst streamers is far more competitive in the US than in Europe. Netflix, Amazon and YouTube have all bought NFL rights, while Apple is investing heavily in Formula One, so I wouldn’t rule any of them out.”
Adam Kelly, president of global sports marketing agency IMG, has a seat at the table at many rights negotiations and has long predicted the rise of the streamers, viewing the 2030 World Cup as the potential tipping point when a premium event could be exclusively bought in a major market by a streaming service for the first time. IMG has the rights to sell more than 70 global sports organisations, including the Premier League, World Rugby and Wimbledon.
In addition to the exclusive rights in the US for the 2027 and 2031 Women’s World Cups, Netflix has secured exclusive 2030 World Cup rights in Spain. It must sub-license all of the Spanish national team’s matches, both semi-finals and final and at least one match per day, to a domestic free-to-air broadcaster to comply with government regulations.
“These [streaming] entities are the future of broadcasting, as they are the best companies in the world at turning attention into earnings,” Kelly says. “Their model allows them to monetise better than their rivals due to their size, scale and the high consumption levels of their customers.
“Netflix in particular has built a sophisticated and lucrative advertising platform. They have the back-office capability and 2027 would provide a perfect test run. If they’re successful in the tender for the World Cup it shows they are potentially the future of sports broadcasting.”
Netflix’s diversification into an advertising business, which brought in $1.5bn last year with projections of $2.7bn this year, puts it ahead of Apple TV and Amazon and well placed to make a profit from an undertaking as large as broadcasting a men’s World Cup. The lack of stipulations in the US for free-to-air coverage makes this tender particularly attractive to Netflix, although if successful it could make some matches available to non-subscribers for promotional purposes, as Apple TV has done with Major League Soccer.
“As a company, Netflix’s unique offering is exclusivity, so why would they hand that to their rivals?” another broadcast source said. “There are no regulations in the US preventing exclusivity so I would expect Netflix to bid for and retain every game if they win.”
Given recent reports that Netflix is exploring tabling an offer for NBC Universal after withdrawing its $85bn bid for Warner Bros last year, a future partnership with a linear network cannot be ruled out if it is successful. TBMM Başkanı Numan Kurtulmuş, Meclis'te Yeni Parti Grubu'nu ziyaret ediyor.
Dünya ve Türk halter tarihinin efsane sporcularından, üst üste 3 olimpiyat şampiyonluğu, 7'şer kez dünya ve Avrupa şampiyonluğu bulunan "Cep Herkülü" lakaplı Naim Süleymanoğlu, 23 Ocak 1967'de Bulgaristan'ın Kırcaali şehrinin Ahatlı köyünde dünyaya geldi.
Naim Süleymanoğlu, haltere başlamasıyla ilgili açıklamasında şöyle demişti:
"9 yaşındayken halter antrenörüm Hilmi (Pekünlü) hoca beni keşfetti, böylece haltere başladım. O zamanlar Bulgaristan'dan dünya ve olimpiyat şampiyonu sporcular çıkıyordu, ben de şampiyon olmak istedim."
Sadece sporcu olarak değil, Bulgaristan'daki Türklerin gördüğü zulmü dünyaya duyurmasıyla tarihe geçen Naim Süleymanoğlu, 14 yaşında Bulgaristan'da gençler ve yıldızlar şampiyonu oldu. 15 yaşında 1982'de Brezilya'da düzenlenen Gençler Dünya Şampiyonası'nda ilk dünya şampiyonluğunu elde eden Süleymanoğlu, "En genç dünya rekortmeni" ünvanına erişmişti.
1983'te Büyükler Dünya Halter Şampiyonası'nda birinci olan Naim Süleymanoğlu, 1983-1986 yılları arasında gençlerde 13, büyüklerde 50 rekor kırdı, 1984, 1985 ve 1986'da dünyada yılın haltercisi seçildi.
ABD'de 1983'te gerçekleştirilen "Rekortmenlerin Turnuvası"na katılan ve burada dünya rekorunu kıran Naim Süleymanoğlu'na, ABD basını tarafından "Cep Herkülü" lakabı takıldı.
Süleymanoğlu, 1984 Los Angeles Olimpiyatları'na Bulgaristan'ın Sovyetler Birliği'nin boykot kararını desteklemesiyle katılamadı.
Öte yandan Naim Süleymanoğlu, 1984 yılında silkme kategorisinde vücut ağırlığının 3 katını kaldıran ikinci halterci olarak tarihe geçti.
Bulgaristan hükümetinin "Soya dönüş operasyonu" kapsamında Türk isimlerini yasaklaması nedeniyle adı Naum Şalamanov olarak değiştirildi.
Türkiye'ye gelişini, kendi ifadesiyle "Türkiye kaçışını", 1980'li yıllarda Bulgaristan'da yaşayan Türklere yapılan zulümlerin dünyaya duyurulması ve bitirilmesine yönelik bir girişim şeklinde açıklayan Naim Süleymanoğlu, o yıllarda Bulgaristan'da Türklerin asimilasyona maruz kaldığını dünyaya duyurmuştu.
"Cep Herkülü", Türkiye'ye geliş süreciyle ilgili, "Türklere karşı yapılan zulümleri kabullenmem mümkün değildi. Türkleri yok sayanlar için ter dökmek istemiyordum. Türkiye'ye iltica edecektim. 1985-1986 şubat ayı sonuna kadar bütün Türklerin isimleri değiştirildi. Artık adım; Naum Şalamanov'du. 1986'da Avustralya'nın Melbourne kentinde düzenlenen Dünya Halter Şampiyonası'nda birinci oldum. Şampiyonanın sonunda 10 Aralık 1986'da verilen akşam yemeğinde beni Türk Konsolosluğuna götürecek kişilerle tanıştım." açıklamasında bulunmuştu.
1986'da Avustralya'da Türk Büyükelçiliğine sığınarak iltica eden Naim Süleymanoğlu, başarılı bir operasyonla Avustralya'dan uçakla Londra'ya geçti. Ardından dönemin başbakanı Turgut Özal'ın gönderdiği özel uçakla Türkiye'ye getirilen Naim Süleymanoğlu, Ankara'da coşkulu bir karşılama ve basın toplantısıyla ilk kez Türk halkının karşısına çıktı.
Naim Süleymanoğlu'nun 1988 Seul Olimpiyatları'na Türkiye adına katılabilmesi için Türk hükümetince Bulgaristan'a 1 milyon dolar ödeme yapıldı.
O tarihten itibaren Naim Süleymanoğlu, şampiyonalarda Türkiye adına mücadele etti. Merhum Cumhurbaşkanı Turgut Özal'ın ödemeyle ilgili, "Naim bize onu kat ve kat ödedi. Dünyada Türklerin reklamını yaptı." ifadesi kayıtlarda yer alıyor.
Naim Süleymanoğlu'nun Türkiye'ye kaçması ile Bulgaristan'da yaşayan Türklere zulmedildiği, sünnetin yasaklandığı, sünnet yaptıranlara hapis cezası verildiği, mezar taşlarındaki isimler nedeniyle mezarların dahi yıkıldığı dünya kamuoyuna duyuruldu.
Dünyanın efsane sporcuları arasına yerleşen Naim Süleymanoğlu, Güney Kore'de düzenlenen 1988 Seul Olimpiyatları'nda erkekler 60 kiloda mücadele ederken, 6 dünya, 9 olimpiyat rekoru kırarak şampiyon oldu.
Ağırlığının 3 katından 10 kilo fazlasını (190 kilo) kaldırarak "Dünyanın en iyi haltercisi" ödülünü kazanan "Cep Herkülü", bunu dünyada başaran tek sporcu olarak tarihe geçti.
Naim ayrıca, silkmenin yanı sıra koparmada da 152,5 kilo kaldırarak toplamda 342,5 kiloya ulaşıp, dünya ve olimpiyat rekorları kırdı.
"Cep Herkülü", olimpiyatlarda güreş dışında Türkiye'ye ilk altın madalyayı getiren sporcu olarak tarihte yerini aldı.
Naim Süleymanoğlu, 1992'de de Uluslararası Halter Basın Komisyonu tarafından dünyanın en iyi sporcusu ilan edildi.
Milli halterci, 1988 Seul, 1992 Barselona ve 1996 Atlanta Olimpiyatları'nda birinci olarak, üst üste 3 olimpiyat altın madalyasıyla podyuma çıktı. Naim Süleymanoğlu, kariyerinde ayrıca 7'şer kez dünya ve Avrupa şampiyonluğuna ulaşırken, 46 dünya rekoruna imza attı.
1996'da haltere ara veren Naim Süleymanoğlu, sonrasında katıldığı 2000 Sidney Olimpiyatları'nda başarılı olamadı ve aktif spor hayatına veda etti. Efsane sporcu, Sydney'e kadar 24 yıl boyunca halterde bir numara olarak adından söz ettirdi.
1988 Seul Olimpiyatları'nda 6 dünya, 9 olimpiyat rekoru kıran ve "Dünyanın en iyi haltercisi" seçilen Naim Süleymanoğlu, 3 Ekim 1988'de "Everybody Wins" başlığıyla Time dergisine kapak oldu.
O yıl Avrupa Halter Şampiyonası'nın ardından dönemin ABD Başkanı Ronald Reagan tarafından Beyaz Saray'a davet edilen Naim Süleymanoğlu, teklif edilen ABD vatandaşlığını ise reddetmişti.
Naim Süleymanoğlu, 2000 yılında Uluslararası Halter Federasyonunda (IWF) dünyanın en genç asbaşkanı oldu. 2012 Londra Olimpiyat Oyunları kapsamında adı, Londra metrosundaki bir istasyona verildi. 2018 yılında Ankara Büyükşehir Belediyesi tarafından Çankaya'da bir caddeye de "Naim Süleymanoğlu" adı verildi.
Türk spor tarihine damga vuran Naim Süleymanoğlu'nun hayatını anlatan, yönetmenliğini Özer Feyzioğlu'nun yaptığı, senaryosunu Barış Pirhasan'ın Naim Süleymanoğlu'nun kardeşi Muharrem Süleymanoğlu'nun anılarını içeren "Kardeşim Cep Herkülü" kitabından yola çıkarak yazdığı "Cep Herkülü: Naim Süleymanoğlu" adlı film, 22 Kasım 2019'da seyirciyle buluştu.
Filmde Naim Süleymanoğlu'nun, 1970'li yıllarda 10 yaşındayken halterle tanışmasından başlayarak 1988 yılındaki Seul Olimpiyatlarına kadar geçen yılları anlatıldı.
Efsane milli halterci, 18 Kasım 2017'de tedavi gördüğü hastanede karaciğer yetmezliği nedeniyle 50 yaşında hayata veda etti. 28 Eylül 2017'de hastaneye kaldırılan Naim Süleymanoğlu ile yakından ilgilenen Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, 9 Ekim 2017'de hastanede efsane sporcuyu ziyaret etmişti.
19 Kasım 2017'de İstanbul Fatih Camisi'nde kılınan cenaze namazına siyaset, iş ve spor camiasından çok sayıda kişinin yanı sıra aktif spor yaptığı dönemde en büyük rakibi olan Yunan Valerios Leonidis de katıldı.
Naim Süleymanoğlu, 9 yıl önce Edirnekapı Mezarlığı'nda ebediyete uğurlandı.

Ermenistan'da canlı yayınlanan bir tartışma programında Gazeteci Boris Murazi ve siyasi analist Harutyun Mkrtchyan, yaşanan tartışmanın ardından yumruk ve tekmeli kavga etti.
Ermenistan'da bir televizyon kanalında yayınlanan tartışma programında yumruklar havada uçuştu. Gazeteci Boris Murazi ve siyasi analist Harutyun Mkrtchyan, ülkedeki siyasi gelişmeleri değerlendirmek üzere geçtiğimiz Cuma günü Ermenistan devlet televizyonunun "Büyük Tartışma" (The Great Debate) adlı programına katıldı. Canlı yayınlanan programda zaman zaman tansiyon yükseldi. Tartışma, Mkrtchyan'ın, gazeteci Murazi'ye Ermenistan'ın eski Cumhurbaşkanı Serj Sarkisyan ile kişisel bir ilişkisi olduğu yönündeki iddiaları sorması üzerine şiddetlendi. Eski cumhurbaşkanını açıkça eleştirdiğini kaydeden Murazi, sorunun kabul edilemez olduğunu belirtti. Karşılıklı hakaretlerin duyulduğu stüdyoda, ikili arasında sinirler daha da gerildi. Birbirinin üzerine yürüyen Mkrtchyan ve Murazi, daha sonra birbirine yumruk ve tekme attı. İkiliyi sunucular ve program ekibi ayırmaya çalıştı.
Bir gün sonra sosyal medya hesabı üzerinden canlı yayın yapan Murazi, olaya değinerek Mkrtchyan'ın sınırı aştığını ifade etti.
Haberler.com'da yer alan yorumlar, kullanıcıların kişisel görüşlerini yansıtır ve haberler.com'un editöryal politikası ile örtüşmeyebilir. Yorumların hukuki sorumluluğu tamamen yazarlarına aittir.

Bordeaux fans protested when the club were demoted to the sixth tier
The latest stop on Zinedine Zidane's homecoming tour was an important one for the new France head coach. When Les Bleus took on Turkey in Bordeaux on Sunday night, the ex-midfielder was returning to the city in which he spent four formative years of his playing career, between 1992 and 1996.
"I became a man in Bordeaux," Zidane fondly recalled in the build-up. France edged triumphed 2-1 with an uninspiring display, but it did not dampen the mood of the 40,000 fans inside the Stade Atlantique.
While the 1998 World Cup winner was not necessarily in familiar surroundings (the out-of-town stadium was built for Euro 2016, 20 years after his departure for Juventus), locals made every effort to make him feel at home, holding up a commemorative tifo before kick-off and chanting Zizou's name throughout.
Just a few miles up the road earlier that afternoon, Zidane's former club were playing their fifth match of the season in the sixth-tier Regional 1, in a north-western suburb of the city.
Thousands of Bordeaux fans had made the short away outing to Saint-Medard-en-Jalles' 3000-seater ground to watch their team seal a fifth win in five this season.
Girondins de Bordeaux, the six-time French champions, who were once regulars in European cups, now find themselves facing amateur opposition on a weekly basis.
Since 2022, the club has plummeted from Ligue 1 to the sixth tier through a combination of on-pitch struggles, mismanagement at all levels, and sanctions due to their financial troubles.
The club was taken over in 2021 by Gerard Lopez, who was previously in charge of Formula 1's Lotus as well as another French side, Lille.
While Bordeaux were already hamstrung by debts at that point, the situation on and off the pitch worsened under the Spanish-Luxembourgish businessman as the men's first team finished rock bottom of Ligue 1 in his first season.
A couple of seasons in Ligue 2 followed, before the club was docked down to the fourth tier in 2024. In their first National 2 season, they notably signed Andy Carroll but ultimately missed out on promotion.
The following campaign saw a repeat of that near miss, and the club was expelled from national-level football altogether this summer over their finances.
With Bordeaux left on the brink and whittled down to just eight full-time employees (down from around 250 a few years beforehand), Lopez sold up to Park Bench, a group of mainly British USA-based investors who also own Scottish side Dunfermline as well as a minority stake in Spanish second tier side Cordoba.
The supporters turned out in their numbers for the first home match of the campaign, which had been delayed amid the uncertainty over whether the club could continue running, against Stade Montois.
More than 11,000 tickets sold, a record crowd for that level of French football.
"140 years of history, we won't be stopped," read one of the banners held up by the Ultramarines fan group, who also made it a point to thank the seven first-team players who had stayed despite the club's double relegation.
The team is centred around a core of players with Ligue 1 and Ligue 2 experience. Steve Shamal, who scored a hat-trick in that 4-1 victory over Stade Montois, previously turned out for the likes of Caen and Annecy in the second tier.
"We know we should be higher up, but that certainty can also be a trap," said Shamal after the game. "We shouldn't think that it's going to be easy.
"We need to respect our opponents if we're going to put in good performances."
As the sixth tier of French football is regionalised, only the league winner in the Nouvelle Aquitaine region's top flight will earn promotion.
Their on-pitch success so far this season comes as little surprise given the gulf in quality compared to the rest of the league. Over the summer, Bordeaux notably managed to hold on to Europa League-winning full-back Almamy Toure, while former Belgian youth international striker Baptiste Guillaume also joined.
Several former players have also looked to get involved in Bordeaux's revival.
Benoit Tremoulinas, the former French international who was a part of the title-winning squad in 2008-09, notably announced that at the age of 40 he would be lacing up his boots again seven years after injury forced him to retire.
Paul Baysse, the former centre-back, is an assistant to head coach Arnaud Cormier.
Benoit Tremoulinas spent six years at Bordeaux, winning a league title and two cups, before also twice winning the Europa League with Sevilla
Perhaps the most significant endorsement the new owners could have hoped for was that of Alain Giresse, widely regarded as the club's greatest player. The Euro 1984 winner, who won three league titles while playing more than 500 times for the Marine et Blanc, was in attendance for the match against Stade Montois. He took the ceremonial kick-off before giving a full-time dressing room speech.
The new management unveiled their long-term plans for the club on Monday at Le Haillan, the city-owned training ground which includes a chateau that hosts the club's headquarters.
"We are humbled to have this responsibility," Park Bench investor Jeremy Green said.
"The club doesn't belong to Park Bench, it belongs to Bordeaux, it belongs to the 11,000 people who came to watch a Regional 1 game, to the players and to the community. We have a responsibility to rebuild this club.
"Our commitment to the community and to the players is that we will be fiscally responsible and patient.
"We're not a financial institution, we're a collection of individuals who bring with them business, sporting, analytical, and entrepreneurship skills."
Dominique Delport, the club's new president, revealed he knew Green and Twining through his wife, who studied at Oxford with them.
"We can learn from the club's golden years," the former journalist and advertising executive told BBC Sport, before adding that he would look to bring club legends to every league game.
While the club was sold for a symbolic euro, it did involve taking on long-standing debts which spanned transfer fees, stadium rent, and a compensation claim by former head coach Vladimir Petkovic.
Last Friday, the city's commercial court approved a request to restructure the debt as part of the club's continuation plan.
When Bordeaux were expelled from national-level football by the French FA at the start of the summer, the club used several avenues to appeal while the takeover was being finalised.
"We thought we had acquired the club in National 1 [the fourth tier]," Green and co-investor James Twining, told BBC Sport.
"Initially we walked away, but we were encouraged to come back," Green added. "We established that we were going to be able to restructure things and make it work.
"People around the club and in the local community encouraged us to try to find a way."
The six-time French champions have a long way to go before returning to the top flight.
"We're committing to a sensible financial structure, to a well-run club, and we're talking about 10 years to get this club back to Ligue 1," the new investors added.
A crucial step towards that long-term goal will be returning to the professional leagues, which would allow them to re-open the youth academy they were made to close when they dropped down.
Rebuilding the women's team, who were involved in the Champions League only a few seasons ago, is another one of the new owners' objectives.
Keeping the fans onside throughout the process will also be key, not least after the rift that opened up between groups during the previous ownership.
In any case, if the record-breaking turnout for Bordeaux's return to league action is anything to go by, their support seems unlikely to waver anytime soon.

Watch our 'Unfinished Business' Transfer Show special on Sky Sports News at 4pm and 7pm as we look ahead to January ; Man Utd are expected to be active in the market with left-back, centre-back and a forward on the agenda for new head coach Mauricio Pochettino
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is expected to be backed in the January transfer window as the club aim to address their disappointing start to the season.
A left-back, centre-back and forward are areas the club are looking to potentially strengthen in January with Pochettino expected to have input on targets they will pursue.
Despite the club's hierarchy feeling the team should be further up the table, there is also an acknowledgement that they could have further strengthened the squad in the summer in areas where they lacked depth.
Sky Sports News understands the club already had plans to move in the upcoming window under former head coach Michael Carrick, before he was sacked last month following United's worst start to a league season for 40 years.
However, Pochettino is now expected to be consulted in the coming weeks and will have his say on potential recruits in January.
Tune in to Sky Sports News at 4pm and 7pm for our 'Unfinished Business' Transfer Show special for in-depth analysis of Man Utd's plans for the January window.
Fulham's Calvin Bassey and Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite are two players United are monitoring as potential options to reinforce their defence in January.
Despite Fulham's struggles this season, Bassey is a player who has impressed and has just six months left on his current deal, though his club have the option to extend that by a further year.
Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa has described the 26-year-old as one of the best defenders in the world and said the club's aim is to extend Bassey's contract.
Meanwhile, Branthwaite has long been admired by United. In 2024, United had two bids rejected for the centre-back, their second being worth around £50m.
Everton are in a strong negotiating position over the 24-year-old, who has a contract until the summer of 2030.
United are looking at left-footed centre-back options as they consider potential replacements for Lisandro Martinez. His future at Old Trafford looks in doubt come next summer with his current contract expiring.
Despite United having an option for a further 12 months, he is unlikely to be offered fresh terms as Sky Sports News reported last month.
The club decided not to pursue a left-back in the summer as they focused on their midfield rebuild with the belief their long-term targets would be more attainable next year.
It remains to be seen whether that will be true come the end of the season and where that leaves players such as Newcastle United's Lewis Hall, but with five different players being used in that position with limited success, the club will look at the possibility of cover at left-back in January.
Fulham left-back Antonee Robinson continues to be monitored, as first reported by Sky Sports News in March. Fulham are aware of widespread interest in Robinson but no club has so far made a move for the 29-year-old, who worked under Pochettino with the USA.
Barcelona's Alejandro Balde was a player linked with United in the summer but was never at a stage when the move seemed likely. United were aware of his potential availability and it has not been ruled out that they revisit a deal in January if it works for all parties.
Manchester City's Rayan Ait-Nouri was an option United tentatively explore on Deadline Day but they decided against pursuing him due to City's insistence on an obligation to make the move permanent. Sky Sports News understands he is not considered a target at this stage as United look at other options.
With United's main No 9 Benjamin Sesko ruled out until at least January, the club will explore potential reinforcements in the upcoming window to re-balance the club's attack.
Although United scored seven goals in their last two games before the break, the club have missed a physical presence in Sesko's absence to lead the line.
Leeds United's Dominic Calvert-Lewin was a player of interest but his future looks likely to remain at Elland Road and United are not expected to explore a move for the forward.
Any outgoings in January could have an impact on how much the club can reinforce Pochettino's squad but numerous first-team departures are not likely with the size of the squad and long-term injuries as well as Pochettino needing time to assess his squad all set to play a factor.
Joshua Zirkzee continues to be a player who attracts interest from Italy and United could entertain a move for the Dutch forward if they receive a suitable offer but would need cover in that position.
Martinez's future will under the spotlight in January. Sky Sports News reported last month United are unlikely to offer him a new contract. His current deal expires next summer although the club hold an option for a further 12 months.
Pochettino will also have to manage other expiring contracts in his squad with Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw and captain Bruno Fernandes also in the last six months of their current contracts, although it is worth noting the club have a 12-month option on Fernandes and Maguire.

Vakıftan yapılan açıklamaya göre, COP31 kapsamında Mavi Alan'daki Kadın Pavilyonu'nda düzenlenen sivil toplum panelinde, TÜRGEV'in uluslararası ortaklarla yürüttüğü çevre ve sürdürülebilirlik projeleri ele alındı.
Panelde, Türkiye ve Litvanya'dan 40 gencin katılımıyla 2022-2023 döneminde gerçekleştirilen "Tohumun Yolculuğu - Sürdürülebilir Tarımda Gençlik Hareketi" projesinde yapılan çalışmalar anlatıldı.
Proje kapsamında gençlerin sürdürülebilir tarım, ata tohumlarının korunması, ekolojik tarım, karbon ayak izi ve biyoçeşitlilik konularında eğitim aldığı, iki ülkede düzenlenen teknik gezilerle çevre dostu tarım uygulamalarını yerinde incelediği aktarıldı.
Türkiye, Fransa ve Yunanistan ortaklığında 2023-2024 döneminde yürütülen "Doğa Kardeşliği" projesinde ise çocukların ve gençlerin çevre bilincini artırmaya yönelik eğitim faaliyetlerinin gerçekleştirildiği anlatıldı.
Panelde ayrıca TÜRGEV'in hamiliğinde kurulan Eğitim ve Gençlik Derneğinin (EGADER), Kuzey Makedonya ve İspanya'dan ortaklarla hazırladığı "ECO-VOICE - Gençlerin Çevre İçin Sesi" projesine ilişkin de bilgi verildi.
Ulusal Ajans'ın değerlendirmesindeki başvurunun kabul edilmesi halinde, 18-30 yaş arasındaki 50 gencin çevre sorunlarına yönelik çözüm önerileri geliştirmesi ve bunları yerel karar alıcılara taşımasının amaçlandığı aktarıldı. Proje kapsamında 2027'de Kuzey Makedonya'nın Kavadarci ve İspanya'nın Barselona kentlerinde buluşmalar planlandığı belirtildi.
Açıklamada görüşlerine yer verilen TÜRGEV Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Hatice Akıncı Yılmaz, iklim değişikliğiyle mücadelede eğitimin önemine dikkati çekti.
Yılmaz, Türkiye'nin 2053 Net Sıfır Emisyon hedefini ortaya koyduğunu, COP31'e ev sahipliği yaparak küresel iklim gündeminde sorumluluk üstlendiğini belirterek, "Hedefleri devletler koyar, onları yarına taşıyan nesillerdir. İklim politikasının en kalıcı yatırımı eğitimdir." ifadelerini kullandı.
Genç kızların uluslararası karar süreçlerinde yer alması gerektiğini vurgulayan Yılmaz, şunları kaydetti:
"İklim müzakerelerinde konuşulan her başlık, yarın bir mühendisin ya da bir diplomatın önüne gelecek. O masalarda kendi değerlerini bilen ve dünyanın dilini konuşan genç kızlarımızı görmek istiyoruz. Türkiye'de ve Litvanya'da tohumun ve toprağın izini süren gençlerimiz bu yolda ilk adımı attı. Hedefimiz, genç kızlarımızın o masalarda sözü ve çözümü olan bir nesil olarak yer alması. TÜRGEV'in işi de bu yolun kapılarını açık tutmaktır."

Kocaelispor'un geçen sezon 16 yıllık Süper Lig özlemine son vermesinin ardından 3 Haziran 2025'te takımın başına getirilen 41 yaşındaki teknik adam, yeşil-siyahlı ekibin geçen sezon ligde kalma mücadelesini başarıyla tamamlamasında önemli rol oynadı.
Süper Lig'de teknik direktör değişikliklerinin sık yaşandığı dönemde koltuğunu koruyan İnan, görev süresi bakımından ligin en istikrarlı üçüncü ismi oldu.
23 Haziran 2022'de Galatasaray'da göreve başlayan Okan Buruk (yaklaşık 4 yıl 5 ay) ve 21 Kasım 2023'te Göztepe ile anlaşan Bulgar çalıştırıcı Stanimir Stoilov'un (yaklaşık 3 yıl) ardından İnan, en uzun süredir aynı takımda görev yapan isim olarak öne çıktı.
Süper Lig'de 2025-26 sezonunda mücadele eden 18 takımdan 13'ü teknik direktör değişikliğine giderken yalnızca 5 ekip sezona başladığı isimle devam etti.
Ligin ilk 11 haftasında 9 kulüp teknik adam değişikliğine giderken toplam 10 çalıştırıcıyla yollar ayrıldı.
Kocaelispor ise Selçuk İnan ile birlikteliğini koruyarak istikrarını bozmadı.
Futbolculuk kariyerindeki başarılarının ardından Galatasaray'da Fatih Terim'in ekibinde yardımcı antrenörlük yaparak teknik adamlığa adım atan İnan, ilk teknik direktörlük deneyimini Kasım 2022'de Kasımpaşa'da yaşadı.
İstanbul ekibinde çıktığı 13 maçta 3 galibiyet, 2 beraberlik ve 8 mağlubiyetle 0,8 puan ortalaması yakaladı.
Mart 2024'te Gaziantep FK'nin başına geçen İnan, kırmızı-siyahlı ekiple çıktığı 48 karşılaşmada 20 galibiyet, 7 beraberlik ve 21 mağlubiyet elde etti. İnan, Gaziantep temsilcisinde maç başına 1,4 puanla kariyerinin en yüksek ortalamasına ulaştı.
Kocaelispor'un başında bugüne dek 51 resmi karşılaşmaya çıkan genç teknik adam, 18 galibiyet, 12 beraberlik ve 21 mağlubiyet aldı.
İnan yönetimindeki yeşil-siyahlılar, 2025-2026 sezonunu 37 puanla 10. sırada tamamlayarak Süper Lig'de tutunmayı başardı.
2026-27 sezonuna da iddialı giriş yapan Körfez ekibi, bu sezon ligin ilk 11 haftasında elde ettiği 6 galibiyet, 1 beraberlik ve 4 mağlubiyetle 19 puan toplayarak maç başına 1,7 puan ortalamasıyla 7. sırada yer aldı.
İnan, Kasımpaşa, Gaziantep FK ve yeşil-siyahlı ekipte toplam 112 karşılaşmada görev yaptı.
Bu maçlarda 41 galibiyet, 21 beraberlik ve 50 mağlubiyet alan İnan'ın takımları 137 gol atıp kalesinde 143 gol gördü.
